# SuperSplat: All Pages

> SuperSplat turns a raw 3D Gaussian splat capture into a shareable scene: clean it in the browser-based SuperSplat Editor, publish it to superspl.at, curate the viewing experience in Studio, and embed it anywhere with the open-source SuperSplat Viewer.

Index: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/llms.txt
Total Documents: 41
Generated: 2026-11-20

================================================================================

## SuperSplat

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat.md

[SuperSplat](https://superspl.at) turns a raw 3D Gaussian Splat capture into a polished, shareable 3D scene. Clean it up in your browser, publish it with one click, and let anyone explore it on any device.

[Interactive demo: Honeybee — a Gaussian splat published and curated on superspl.at](https://superspl.at/s?id=3ae6a716)

Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and click the numbered hotspots. This honeybee by [danylyon](https://superspl.at/user/danylyon) was cleaned in the [Editor](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor.md), published to [superspl.at](https://superspl.at), and annotated in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md). Everything on this page is about doing the same with your own captures.

## SuperSplat in 60 seconds

[Video: SuperSplat: Edit, Publish and Share 3D Gaussian Splats](https://www.youtube.com/embed/7B0KdoJCUK8)

Browse, view, clean up, publish, curate, convert, and share: the whole platform in under a minute.

## Where do you want to start?

[🧹 I have a splat file](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/getting-started.md): Clean up floaters, crop the scene, and publish it from the browser-based Editor. Follow the quick start and you'll have a shareable scene page in about ten minutes. Getting Started →
[🎬 I've published a splat](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md): Make it shine in Studio: frame the opening camera, keyframe a flythrough, add annotated hotspots, dial in bloom and color grading, set a skybox, or make the scene walkable with collision. Studio →
[🧩 I want splats on my own site or app](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md): Embed the open-source Viewer with an iframe, export a single-file HTML viewer to host yourself, or publish from your own pipeline with the API. Viewer, embedding and API →
[📷 I don't have a splat yet](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/gaussian-splatting/creating.md): Learn how a splat is captured and trained, and pick a tool that fits you, from one-tap phone apps to desktop trainers. Then come back here with your first PLY. Creating Splats →

:::tip Already have a clean splat?

You can skip the Editor. Hit the orange **Upload Splat** button on the [superspl.at home page](https://superspl.at) or use [Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md) to publish a ready-made file straight to your [Manage page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md).

:::

## How the pieces fit together

Some parts of SuperSplat you use as a creator, some your visitors use to view what you've made, and some are general-purpose utilities.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph you [You: create and publish]
        direction LR
        raw([Splat file]) --> editor([Editor])
        raw --> upload([Direct Upload])
        editor --> manage([Manage])
        upload --> manage
        manage <--> studio([Studio])
    end

    manage --> scene(["Scene page (hosts Viewer)"])

    subgraph visitors [Visitors: discover and view]
        direction LR
        explore([Explore]) <--> scene
        profile([User Profile]) <--> scene
    end
```

| Surface | What it is | Where it lives |
|---------|------------|----------------|
| **[Editor](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor.md)** | Browser-based editor for cleaning, cropping, color-adjusting, and animating splats. Publishes to superspl.at. | [superspl.at/editor](https://superspl.at/editor) |
| **[Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md)** | Publish an already-clean splat file without opening the Editor. | The orange **Upload Splat** button on [superspl.at](https://superspl.at) |
| **[Manage](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md)** | Your splat library: edit title and description, change visibility, choose downloadable + license, delete, open in Studio. | [superspl.at/manage](https://superspl.at/manage) |
| **[Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md)** | Curate the published viewing experience: look and tone, skybox, cameras, camera animation, collision, post effects, annotations. | `superspl.at/scene/<hash>/studio` |
| **[Scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md)** | Public page for a published splat: embedded viewer, share, embed, download, comments, likes, suggested splats. | `superspl.at/scene/<hash>` |
| **[Explore](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/explore.md)** | Public gallery with sort, time, feature filters, and search. The superspl.at home page. | [superspl.at](https://superspl.at) |
| **[User Profile](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/user-profile.md)** | A creator's public page: avatar, bio, social links, their published splats. | `superspl.at/user/<username>` |
| **[Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md)** | The open-source web viewer that powers scene pages and Editor HTML exports. Embed it in your own page or self-host it. | npm `@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer`, [GitHub](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-viewer) |
| **[Convert](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/convert.md)** | Web frontend to the [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) CLI: convert formats, transform, and filter in the browser. | [superspl.at/convert](https://superspl.at/convert) |
| **[API & Integrations](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/api-integrations.md)** | Publish and inspect scenes from capture tools, training pipelines, and custom applications. | [API reference](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/api/supersplat/) |

## Good to know

- **Everything runs in your browser.** The Editor loads splats locally and nothing is uploaded until you choose to publish. It needs a [browser with WebGPU](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor.md#system-requirements).
- **Browsing is anonymous.** A free PlayCanvas account is needed to publish, like, or comment. See [Account Creation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/account-management/user-accounts/account-creation.md).
- **Open source at the core.** The [Editor](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat), the [Viewer](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-viewer), and [splat-transform](https://github.com/playcanvas/splat-transform) (which powers Convert) are MIT-licensed. Studio, Manage, Explore, scene pages, and the publish API are hosted by PlayCanvas on superspl.at.
- **Publishing optimizes for you.** Every published splat is compressed to SOG, and splats over one million Gaussians are streamed progressively so they load fast on any device. See [Streaming & Performance](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md).
- **You can host it yourself.** Export a single-file HTML viewer from the Editor or use the Viewer npm package. See [Self-Hosting the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md).

## Stay in the loop

- [SuperSplat news on the PlayCanvas blog](https://blog.playcanvas.com/tags/supersplat/)

- [GitHub](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat) for issues and contributions

## Getting Started

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/getting-started/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/getting-started.md

This guide takes a raw splat file all the way to a published, shareable scene page. It takes about ten minutes and touches every part of the SuperSplat workflow: **Editor → Publish → Studio → Share**.

## Before you start

- **A splat file.** Any `.ply` produced by a Gaussian splatting trainer works, as do `.compressed.ply`, `.sog`, `.splat`, `.ksplat`, `.spz`, and XGRIDS `.lcc` files. Don't have one yet? [Creating Splats](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/gaussian-splatting/creating.md) explains how captures are made and [Recommended Tools](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/gaussian-splatting/creating/recommended-tools.md) compares the apps that produce them. Or practice on the sample biker: [open it in the Editor](https://superspl.at/editor?load=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/willeastcott/assets/main/biker.ply).
- **A free PlayCanvas account** for step 3. Loading and editing don't need one; publishing does. See [Account Creation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/account-management/user-accounts/account-creation.md).
- **A browser with WebGPU.** See the Editor's [System Requirements](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor.md#system-requirements). There is nothing to install.

## 1. Load your splat in the Editor

Open [superspl.at/editor](https://superspl.at/editor) and drop your file anywhere in the window. You can also use **File → Import**.

[Image: The SuperSplat Editor interface]

Once the splat appears, get your bearings:

| Do this | To |
|---------|----|
| Left-drag | Orbit around the focal point |
| Right-drag | Pan |
| Mouse wheel | Zoom |
| Double-click | Set the focal point |
| Press <kbd>F</kbd> | Focus the camera on the current selection |

If the scene is on its side or upside down, select it in the **Scene Manager** and rotate it upright with the transform controls. See [Transform, Measure and Align](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md). The full list of controls is in [Camera Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md).

## 2. Clean it up

Most raw captures contain **floaters**: stray Gaussians hanging in space where the trainer wasn't sure what it saw. Removing them is the single biggest quality win.

1. Turn off **X-Ray** on the mode strip at the top right of the viewport (or press <kbd>N</kbd>) so selections stop at the visible surface, and turn on **Markers** (or press <kbd>Tab</kbd>) to show the Gaussian centers.
2. Pick a selection tool from the toolbar: **Brush Selection** to paint over floaters, **Sphere Brush** to paint in 3D along a surface, **Sphere Selection** or **Box Selection** to grab a 3D region, or **Flood Selection** for an isolated patch. Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> to add to the selection and <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> to remove from it.
3. Press <kbd>Delete</kbd>. Rotate the camera, check from another angle, and repeat.
4. Removed too much? Use **Edit → Undo**, or **Select → Reset Splat** to restore every deleted Gaussian.

[Image: Selected Gaussians highlighted among the centers of the rest]

To crop away everything outside your subject, select the region to keep with Box or Sphere Selection, choose **Select → Invert**, and delete. [Selection and Cleanup](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md) covers every tool plus more cleanup recipes, and [Color and Appearance](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/color-and-appearance.md) is where you fix exposure and tint.

:::tip Save your work

Choose **File → Save** to keep an `.ssproj` project file. It preserves your edits and project setup so you can pick up where you left off. See [Managing Projects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/managing-projects.md).

:::

## 3. Publish

1. Make sure you are logged in at [superspl.at](https://superspl.at) (the **Login** button in the top right). Your avatar appears there when you are.
2. Frame your favorite view. The published scene opens with the camera exactly where you leave it.
3. Choose **File → Publish**, give the splat a **Title** and a **Description**, and click **Publish**.

[Image: The Publish dialog]

Compression to SOG takes a moment, and several minutes for very large scenes. When it finishes, a dialog shows the URL of your new [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md). New splats are **Unlisted**: anyone with the link can view them, but they won't appear in Explore until you make them Public in step 5.

:::tip Already clean?

If your file needs no editing, skip the Editor. The orange **Upload Splat** button on superspl.at publishes it directly. See [Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md).

:::

Every option in the dialog, including republishing to an existing scene, is covered in [Publishing from the Editor](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/editor.md).

## 4. Curate it in Studio

Your splat now appears on your [Manage page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md). Click **Open in Studio** in its row, or **Edit in Studio** on your scene page, to open [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md), where you shape what visitors see.

[Image: The Manage page]

Three things worth doing on a first pass:

- **Frame the opening shot.** In the **Scene** tab, under **Cameras**, frame your best angle and click **Set camera to current view** so visitors start there. See [Cameras](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md).
- **Add a hotspot.** Frame a detail, press <kbd>C</kbd>, click the spot you want to annotate, and give it a title and some text. Visitors click through hotspots like a guided tour. See [Annotations](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md).
- **Add some polish.** Pick a **Tonemapping** curve under **Look & Tone**, or try a **Vignette** or some **Color Grading** under **Post Effects**. See [Look & Tone](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md) and [Post Effects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects.md).

[Video](https://developer.playcanvas.com/video/supersplat-studio-edit-camera.mp4)

Click **Save** in the header when you're happy. Edits are not saved automatically. Each save publishes the complete settings, so visitors see the update as soon as they reload.

## 5. Share it

Open your [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) at `superspl.at/scene/<hash>`.

[Image: A published scene page]

- **Share** copies the link or posts it to social platforms.
- **Embed** gives you an `<iframe>` snippet for your own website. Later Studio changes show up there automatically.
- To let visitors download your splat, enable **Downloadable** and pick a Creative Commons license on the [Manage page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md).
- To appear in [Explore](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/explore.md) and in search results, switch **Visibility** to **Public** in Manage.

## Where next?

- [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/keyboard-shortcuts.md) to speed up cleanup.
- [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md) to animate the camera and publish a flythrough.
- [Collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md) to make a scene walkable in first person.
- [Convert](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/convert.md) to change formats or shrink a splat without leaving the browser.
- [Self-Hosting the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md) to export a single HTML file you can host anywhere.
- [API & Integrations](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/api-integrations.md) to publish from your own pipeline.

## SuperSplat Editor

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor.md

The [SuperSplat Editor](https://superspl.at/editor) is the open-source, browser-based editor at the heart of the [SuperSplat platform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat.md). It's the tool you use to clean up raw splat captures, trim floaters, crop scenes, retouch colors, build camera animations, and publish a finished splat ready to share. The Editor is [open source on GitHub](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat) under the MIT license and runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded until you choose to publish.

If your splat is already clean, you can skip the Editor and [upload it directly](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md).

[Image: SuperSplat Interface]

## Video Tutorials

### Introduction to SuperSplat

A great way to learn the basics of the SuperSplat Editor is to watch this video introduction:

[Video: SuperSplat Basics](https://www.youtube.com/embed/MwzaEM2I55I)

### In-Depth Tutorial

For a more comprehensive guide to using the SuperSplat Editor, check out this in-depth tutorial:

[Video: SuperSplat In-Depth Tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/embed/J37rTieKgJ8)

## System Requirements

- **A WebGPU-capable browser** — Current Chrome or Edge, Safari 26 or later, or Firefox with WebGPU enabled. If WebGPU is unavailable, the Editor shows a message at startup instead of loading.
- **GPU acceleration** — Keep hardware acceleration enabled in your browser. A dedicated GPU helps with very large splats.
- **Nothing to install** — Everything runs in the browser. You can optionally install the Editor as an app from the browser's address bar; it then opens `.ply`, `.splat`, `.sog`, `.spz`, `.ksplat`, and `.ssproj` files directly from your file manager.

## What's next?

- New to SuperSplat? [Getting Started](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/getting-started.md) takes a splat from import to a published scene in about ten minutes
- Get oriented with the [Interface Overview](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md)
- Learn the supported [Import and Export](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/import-export.md) formats
- Clean a capture with [Selection and Cleanup](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md), then use [Transform, Measure and Align](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md) to prepare it
- Work with multiple captures using [Managing Splats](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/scene-management.md), and finish their look with [Color and Appearance](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/color-and-appearance.md)
- Keep the [Keyboard Shortcuts](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/keyboard-shortcuts.md) reference nearby, or check [Troubleshooting](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/troubleshooting.md) when a workflow does not behave as expected
- Once your splat is clean, [Publish](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/editor.md) it to superspl.at to land on your [Manage page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md) and open it in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md)
- Let an AI agent inspect and edit your scene through the browser's experimental [WebMCP](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/webmcp.md) tools

## Interface Overview

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md

The SuperSplat Editor's interface appears as follows:

[Image: The SuperSplat Editor interface with its main areas labeled]

## Interface Elements

The key elements of the interface are labeled:

### Menu Bar

The Menu Bar gives you access to the most commonly used functions in the SuperSplat Editor. The SuperSplat logo at its left edge takes you back to [superspl.at](https://superspl.at).

* **File Menu:** Create, open, and save `.ssproj` projects; import splats, including an **Import Recent** list; export to the supported formats and repeat the last export with **Re-export**; publish to superspl.at.
* **Edit Menu:** Undo or redo changes, or duplicate or separate selected Gaussians into a new splat.
* **Select Menu:** Select all, none, or the inverse; **Lock Selection**, **Unlock All**, **Delete Selection**, and **Reset Splat** to restore deleted Gaussians.
* **Render Menu:** Render an image or a video of your currently loaded scene.
* **Help Menu:** Video tutorials, this user guide, the keyboard shortcuts reference, community links, and **About SuperSplat**.

### Scene Manager

The Scene Manager lists the imported splats in the project. Click a row to choose the active splat, use the eye icons or Solo mode to control visibility, and use the collapsible **Transform** and **Colors** sections below the list for precise transforms and color grading. Right-click a section header or row to copy or paste its values. See [Managing Splats](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/scene-management.md) for the complete workflow.

### Viewport

The 3D viewport where you can visually edit your scenes. A grid helps you orient yourself in the scene. By default the grid lies in the XZ plane (with the world Y axis pointing upwards); the [Overlays](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#overlays) popup can draw the XY and YZ planes as well, in any combination. The X axis is colored red and the Z axis is blue. The grid uses meters, and its divisions adapt to your distance from the scene: 1 meter and 10 cm lines up close, with 100 m and 1 km lines appearing on large scenes.

### View Cube

The View Cube is a gizmo that gives added control over the viewport camera. You can click on any of the circles to switch to an orthographic view of the scene from one of six directions. This can make it easier to make accurate selections in certain circumstances.

### Mode Strip

[Image: The mode strip, with Centers and Rings, Markers, and X-Ray]

The small icon strip beside the View Cube decides what you see and what a selection hits. Its buttons have no labels; hover one for its name, shortcut, and a short description. From left to right:

| Control | Shortcut | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Centers** / **Rings** | <kbd>M</kbd> | Centers | The editing mode: selections pick Gaussians by their center points or by their footprints. Switching mode also turns **Markers** on. |
| **Markers** | <kbd>Tab</kbd> | Off | Shows the center or ring markers on the unselected Gaussians. When off, the scene renders plainly and selected Gaussians keep their indicators. |
| **X-Ray** | <kbd>N</kbd> | On | Selects through all depths. Turn it off to select only the visible surface. |

Press and hold **Centers** or **Rings** for that marker's size and its **Splat Colors** switch, or press and hold **Markers** for **Markers Only**, **Tint Selection**, and **Outline Selection**. See [Selection Mode and X-Ray](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md#selection-mode-and-x-ray) and [Markers and Selection Display](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/color-and-appearance.md#appearance).

### Right Toolbar

This vertical toolbar contains, from top to bottom:

* **Overlays** (eye icon) — opens the [Overlays](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#overlays) popup: grid, bounding box, camera poses, camera info, and diagnostics.
* **Orbit Camera** / **Fly Camera** — a two-option switch for the [camera control mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md) (<kbd>V</kbd>).
* **Frame Selection** (<kbd>F</kbd>) and **Reset Camera** (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd>).
* **Preferences** (gear icon) — opens the [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences) popup.

Only one of the Overlays and Preferences popups is open at a time.

### Bottom Toolbar

This horizontal toolbar contains, from left to right:

* **Undo** and **Redo**.
* The 2D selection tools: **Rectangle**, **Brush**, **Polygon** / **Lasso**, and **Eyedropper** / **Flood**. The last two buttons each hold a pair of tools: click to use the current one, or press and hold to switch to the other.
* The 3D selection tools: **Sphere Brush**, **Sphere Selection**, and **Box Selection**.
* **Move**, **Rotate**, and **Scale**.
* **Measure** and **Orient**, followed by the **Use Local Orientation** toggle (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>) and **Reset Pivot**.

How the selection tools decide what they hit is set on the [Mode Strip](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#mode-strip). See [Selection and Cleanup](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md) and [Transform, Measure and Align](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md).

### Status Bar

The bar along the bottom edge opens the **Timeline** (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd>) and **Splat Data** (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>D</kbd>) panels and shows live counts of the active splat's **Splats**, **Selected**, **Locked**, and **Deleted** Gaussians. The Editor version is shown in the bottom-right corner of the viewport; click it to open the **About** dialog, which also lists your GPU and the versions of the PlayCanvas Engine, Splat Transform, and PCUI that the Editor uses.

### Animation Timeline

The Timeline allows you to create and delete keyframes for the viewport camera. It also allows you to play back (or scrub through) the animation you have configured, along with any [splat sequences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md#splat-sequences) you have imported.

### Splat Data Panel

This panel visualizes the Gaussian data in the active splat as a histogram and lets you select ranges of values. See the [Splat Data panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/data-panel.md).

## Overlays

The **Overlays** popup (the eye icon in the [Right Toolbar](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#right-toolbar)) holds viewport helpers and diagnostics. Each row is a toggle; click anywhere on the row to flip it.

[Image: The Overlays popup]

| Section | Control | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Helpers | **Grid** (<kbd>G</kbd>) | On | Shows the reference grid. |
| | **Planes** | XZ | Which grid planes are drawn: **XZ**, **XY**, and **YZ**, in any combination. The choice is saved with your preferences and in `.ssproj` projects. |
| | **Bounding Box** | On | Draws the bounding box of the active splat. |
| | **Dimensions** | Off | Labels the bounding box edges with their lengths in the viewport, and the [Measure](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md#measure-and-rescale-a-splat) tool's line with its length. |
| | **Camera Poses** | Off | Draws a camera gizmo at every [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md) keyframe. |
| | **Camera Info** (<kbd>I</kbd>) | Off | Shows the editable [camera position and target overlay](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md#camera-info-overlay). |
| Diagnostics | **Frame Timings** | Off | Live GPU and CPU frame times (median, minimum, and 95th percentile over the last second) with a graph, and whether the last frame was rendered sorted or stochastic. |
| | **Overdraw** | Off | Replaces the image with a heat map of how many Gaussians overlap each pixel, with a legend from 1 to over 1000. Red-to-white regions are where cleanup would help performance most. |

Click the reset icon in the popup's header to restore the Overlays defaults.

## Preferences

The **Preferences** popup (the gear icon in the [Right Toolbar](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#right-toolbar)) holds application-wide settings. They are saved in your browser and restored the next time you open the Editor. Hover a setting's name for a short description of what it does.

[Image: The Preferences popup]

| Section | Setting | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| | **Language** | Automatic | Interface language. See [Language](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#language). |
| Rendering | **Tone Mapping** | Linear | Viewport tone mapping curve: Linear, Neutral, ACES, ACES2, Filmic, or Hejl. |
| | **SH Bands** | 3 | Spherical harmonic bands evaluated in the viewport (0–3). Lower values render faster and preview how a reduced-band export will look. |
| | **Min Splat Size** | 2 | Hides Gaussians that project smaller than this many pixels on screen (0–5), which speeds up large scenes. Lower it if small Gaussians leave gaps; values of 1.5 or less hide nothing. This affects the Editor viewport only: exported viewers always use 2. |
| | **Anti-Aliasing** | Auto | For splats trained with anti-aliasing, such as Mip-Splatting. Without it, they draw too bright. **Auto** follows the anti-aliasing tag stored in each file; **On** and **Off** override it for every splat. Unlike the other settings, this is saved with the project rather than as a preference, and a new scene starts at Auto. Exports are tagged to match what the viewport shows. |
| | **Sort Mode** | Radial | The order in which Gaussians are blended. **Radial** sorts by distance from the camera, which stays stable when the camera turns in place. **Depth** sorts along the view direction. Orthographic views always sort by depth. |
| | **Stochastic Alpha** | Auto | How heavy scenes are drawn while you move the camera. **Disabled** always draws depth-sorted, blended frames. **Enabled** always uses stochastic transparency, which needs no sorting and stays responsive on very large scenes at some cost in image quality. **Movement** uses stochastic frames only while the camera or a tool is moving and draws an exact sorted frame once the view settles. **Auto** keeps drawing sorted frames until one proves slow, then behaves like Movement. |
| Camera | **Field of View** | 85° | Field of view of the viewport camera (10°–120°), measured across the viewport's longer side. See [Camera Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md#camera-settings). |
| | **Fly Speed** | 1 | Speed of WASD navigation in fly mode (0.1–30). |
| | **FOV Auto Dolly** | Off | Move the camera as the field of view changes so the subject keeps its framing. See [Camera Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md#camera-settings). |
| Colors | **Background Color** | Black | The viewport background. Also the default background of [published](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/editor.md) scenes and exported viewers. |
| | **Selected Color** | Yellow | The color of selected Gaussians' markers, the selection tint and outline, and the selected bars in the [Splat Data](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/data-panel.md) histogram. |
| | **Unselected Color** | Blue | The color of unselected Gaussians' markers (unless they show **Splat Colors**) and the unselected bars in the histogram. |
| | **Locked Color** | Black, 5% opacity | Applied to [locked](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md#lock-delete-and-restore) Gaussians. The default leaves them dark and almost transparent. |

The four colors are the swatches in the **Colors** row; hover a swatch for its name. Loading an `.ssproj` project applies the view and camera settings saved in that project for the current session without replacing your stored preferences. Selecting **File > New** reapplies your preferences. To restore the factory settings, click the reset icon in the popup's header (**Reset to Defaults**). This also returns the interface language to **Automatic**. The Overlays popup has its own reset button.

### Language

SuperSplat's interface is available in several languages. By default it follows your browser's language — the **Automatic** setting — but you can choose a specific language from the **Language** dropdown at the top of the **Preferences** popup (the gear icon in the [Right Toolbar](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#right-toolbar)).

Switching language takes effect immediately. There is no page reload, so your loaded scene and any unsaved work are preserved. Your choice is remembered across sessions until you change it again or switch back to **Automatic**.

The following languages are supported:

* English — `en`
* Deutsch (German) — `de`
* Español (Spanish) — `es`
* Français (French) — `fr`
* 日本語 (Japanese) — `ja`
* 한국어 (Korean) — `ko`
* Português (Brasil) (Brazilian Portuguese) — `pt-BR`
* Русский (Russian) — `ru`
* 中文 (简体) (Simplified Chinese) — `zh-CN`

:::tip Share a link in a specific language

Add a `?lng=` query parameter set to one of the language codes listed above (for example, `?lng=ja`) to pin the language for a shared link. This overrides both your saved choice and the browser default, so the link always opens in that language.

:::

:::tip Missing your language?

SuperSplat is [open source](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat), and its translations are plain JSON files under [`static/locales`](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat/tree/main/static/locales). [Open an issue](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat/issues) to request a new language, or open a pull request adding or improving a locale file.

:::

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Import and Export

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/import-export/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/import-export.md

Import brings splats into the Editor from capture apps, trainers, and other tools. Export writes the visible splats to a file: a compressed format for the web, a full-quality PLY for archiving, or a standalone HTML viewer to host yourself.

## Supported File Formats

SuperSplat supports several Gaussian Splat scene formats, plus COLMAP and INRIA camera poses for creating timeline keyframes:

| Format | Import | Export | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ------ | ----------- |
| `.ply` | ✅ | ✅ | Standard PLY format - most common interchange format, widely supported but heavyweight |
| `.compressed.ply` | ✅ | ✅ | Compressed PLY format - far smaller than uncompressed PLY, quantizes data. [Learn more](https://blog.playcanvas.com/compressing-gaussian-splats/) |
| `.sog` | ✅ | ✅ | Bundled super-compressed format (a zip file containing `meta.json` and `.webp` textures). Recommended for runtime applications |
| `meta.json` | ✅ | ❌ | Unbundled super-compressed format (accompanied by `.webp` textures). Use [SplatTransform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) CLI tool to export |
| `lod-meta.json` | ✅ | ❌ | [Streamed SOG](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md) bundle (accompanied by per-LOD `.sog` chunks). Use [SplatTransform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) CLI tool to export |
| `.splat` | ✅ | ✅ | Legacy compressed splat format (antimatter15) - less efficient than compressed PLY |
| `.ksplat` | ✅ | ❌ | KSplat compressed splat format. Import only |
| `.spz` | ✅ | ✅ | Niantic compressed format. Exports as SPZ version 4 by default, with SPZ version 3 available for older readers |
| `.lcc` / `.lcc2` | ✅ | ❌ | XGRIDS proprietary multi-LOD formats. SuperSplat asks which level of detail to load |
| `images.txt` | ✅ | ❌ | Camera poses from a [COLMAP reconstruction](https://colmap.github.io/format.html#images-txt). Importing the file creates [Timeline keyframes](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md#importing-camera-poses-as-keyframes); it does not load a splat scene |
| Camera pose `.json` | ✅ | ❌ | Camera poses in the INRIA JSON format. Importing the file creates [Timeline keyframes](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md#importing-camera-poses-as-keyframes); it does not load a splat scene |
| `.html` | ❌ | ✅ | Self-contained viewer app with the compressed splat data embedded in one HTML file |
| `.zip` | ❌ | ✅ | Viewer package containing an HTML app and a separate bundled SOG file (`index.sog`) |

:::warning

Only `.ply` files containing 3D Gaussian Splat data can be loaded - other PLY file types will fail to import.

:::

## Importing Splats

SuperSplat can import Gaussian Splat scenes in `.ply`, `.compressed.ply`, `.splat`, `.ksplat`, `.spz`, `.lcc`, `.lcc2`, `.sog` (bundled SOG), `meta.json` (unbundled SOG), and `lod-meta.json` (Streamed SOG) formats, and animated splats as PLY sequences. It can also import COLMAP `images.txt` and INRIA camera pose `.json` files to create [camera animation keyframes](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md#importing-camera-poses-as-keyframes).

There are four ways to load a Gaussian Splat file:

1. **Drag and drop** - Drop one or more splat files, or a whole folder, from your file system into SuperSplat's window. While you drag files over the window, a **Drop files to import** card lists the accepted formats. While a dialog or progress screen is open, the card does not appear and the drop is refused. For multi-file formats (such as `.lcc`, `.lcc2`, unbundled SOG, or Streamed SOG), drag the parent folder containing those files.
2. **File menu** - Select `File` > `Import` and choose one or more splat files from your file system. `File` > `Import Recent` lists the files and folders you have imported before so you can reload them without browsing for them again; `Clear Recent` at the bottom of the list empties it.
3. **Direct file opening** - If you have installed SuperSplat as an app from your browser's address bar, you can double-click a `.ply`, `.splat`, `.sog`, `.spz`, `.ksplat`, or `.ssproj` file in File Explorer (Windows) or Finder (macOS) to open it in the Editor.
4. **URL loading** - Use the `load` query parameter in the form: `https://superspl.at/editor?load=<SPLAT_URL>`. For example:

    https://superspl.at/editor?load=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/willeastcott/assets/main/biker.ply

    This is particularly useful for sharing splats with others on social platforms like X and LinkedIn.

    The imported splat is named after the last part of the URL path. Add a `filename` parameter to choose the name instead, for example `?load=<SPLAT_URL>&filename=garden.ply`. The file format is taken from `filename`, so it is required when a signed or extensionless URL does not end in the format's extension. Repeat `load` (and `filename`, in the same order) to import several files.

    URL loading also supports multi-file `.lcc`, `.lcc2`, unbundled SOG, and Streamed SOG scenes. Keep their related chunk or texture files at the relative paths referenced by the container.

While a splat loads, a progress dialog shows each file as it is read, followed by the **Sorting** and **Uploading** stages.

### Importing Several Files

A single file, or the files of one multi-file model (such as an unbundled SOG folder), imports straight away. Anything else you pick, drop, or reload from **Import Recent** (several splats, a PLY sequence, or a mix of splats, projects, and camera poses) is sorted into groups and listed in an **Import Files** dialog, one row per group:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Files** | The file name, the main file of a multi-file model, or a sequence's frame range, such as `frame_000[1-5].ply`. |
| **Import** | Whether to import the row. Every row is ticked by default; unsupported files are listed but cannot be imported. |
| **As** | How the row imports: **Scene** for a splat or multi-file model, **Project** for an `.ssproj` file, **Camera poses** for COLMAP or INRIA pose files, or **Not supported**. A PLY sequence offers a choice of **Sequence** (the default) or one scene per frame, shown with the frame count (for example **120 scenes**), which imports every frame as a separate splat. |

Click **Import** to import the ticked rows, or **Cancel** to import nothing. Projects are listed first, because opening one replaces the current scene.

### Choosing a Level of Detail

When a file contains multiple levels of detail, SuperSplat displays a **Load Options** dialog before allocating the Gaussians. The dialog lists each LOD and its Gaussian count. It initially selects the most detailed level containing fewer than 20 million Gaussians, helping large scenes avoid excessive memory use.

Choose the LOD that fits your editing needs and available memory, then click **Load**. Lower-detail levels load faster and consume less memory. Click **Cancel** to stop the import without loading a level.

### Importing PLY Sequences

SuperSplat can play animated Gaussian Splats on the [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md), where each frame of the animation is a complete splat stored in its own PLY file.

To import a PLY sequence:

1. Ensure your PLY (or `.compressed.ply`) files share a folder and a filename prefix, followed by sequential frame numbers, such as:
   - `animation_0001.ply`
   - `animation_0002.ply`
   - `animation_0003.ply`
   - etc.

2. Load the sequence into SuperSplat by either:
   - **Dragging and dropping** all the PLY files from your file system into SuperSplat
   - **Dragging and dropping** a folder containing the PLY files onto SuperSplat
   - Using **File > Import** and selecting multiple PLY files

3. In the [Import Files](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/import-export.md#importing-several-files) dialog, the frames appear as a single row named by their frame range. Leave **As** set to **Sequence** and click **Import**.

Once loaded, the sequence appears as one splat in the Scene Manager and the [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md) panel drives it, allowing you to:

- Step through frames using the arrow buttons
- Play the animation using the play button
- Scrub through the animation using the timeline slider

You can import several sequences, and they play together. See [Splat Sequences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md#splat-sequences).

:::note

Sequences are memory-intensive since each frame loads a complete splat scene. For optimal performance, consider the file sizes and number of frames when working with animated splats.

:::

## Exporting Splats

To export your currently loaded scene, open the `File` > `Export` submenu and choose **PLY**, **SOG**, **SPZ**, **Splat**, or **Viewer App**. Exports include the visible splats only. Every export uses the same dialog:

[Image: The export dialog with its Location and Filename rows]

- **Location** - The output folder. The Editor remembers the folder you last exported to; click **Choose output folder…** (or **Change…**) to pick another. In browsers without the File System Access API this row is hidden and the file is delivered as a download instead.
- **Filename** - The name of the output file. The dialog warns if the name is invalid or already exists in the folder (the button then reads **Overwrite**), and it refuses to overwrite a file that the current scene is still reading from.
- Format-specific options:
  - **PLY**: **Compress PLY** writes a `.compressed.ply` instead of a full-size PLY; **SH Bands** chooses how many spherical harmonic bands to include.
  - **SOG**: **SH Bands**, and **Iterations** (1–20, default 10), the number of clustering passes used to compress the spherical harmonic data. More iterations give slightly better quality at the cost of export time.
  - **SPZ**: **SH Bands**, and **Version**. **SPZ 4** (the latest version of the spec) is the default, while **SPZ 3** (legacy gzip container) is available for compatibility with older third-party SPZ readers.
  - **Viewer App**: the options for a standalone HTML viewer are described in [Self-Hosting the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md).

**SH Bands** (0–3) is the exact number of spherical harmonic bands written. It starts at the highest band count in the scene, capped by the **SH Bands** setting in [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences), so a default export keeps what the viewport shows. Choosing more bands than a splat contains fills the missing coefficients with zeros. This lets you export a band-0 splat with 3 bands for tools that expect a fixed spherical harmonic layout.

The suggested filename is the splat's name with its extension, in upper or lower case, replaced by the export format's: a splat loaded from `Garden.PLY` is suggested as `Garden.sog` for a SOG export.

Choose `File` > `Re-export` (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd>) to repeat the last export with the same options to the same file. It overwrites the previous output without further prompts, which is handy while iterating on a cleanup.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Managing Projects

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/managing-projects/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/managing-projects.md

SuperSplat supports the `.ssproj` file format, allowing you to save and reload your work, preserving all settings and animations. This format provides an efficient way to manage projects, share work, and continue editing at a later time.

## Features of `.ssproj` Files

* Full Project Save: Stores every imported splat with its edits, transform, pivot, and applied color grades, plus the camera, view settings such as the grid planes and the [Anti-Aliasing](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences) setting, and the timeline animation.
* Easy Reloading: Load a saved project file to restore the exact state of your work.
* Portability: Share `.ssproj` files with others to collaborate on projects.

## Saving a Project

To save your current work as a `.ssproj` file:

* Open the `File` menu and select `Save As`.
* In the **Save As** dialog, choose the output folder under **Location**. The Editor remembers the last folder you used; click **Choose output folder…** (or **Change…**) to pick another.
* Enter a **Filename**. The dialog warns if a file of that name already exists and offers to **Overwrite** it.
* Click **Save**. Your project will be stored as a `.ssproj` file.

Once a project has a name, `File` > `Save` writes to the same file again without asking. In browsers without the File System Access API, the project is delivered as a download instead.

## Loading a Project

To load a previously saved `.ssproj` file:

* Open the `File` menu and select `Open`, then browse to the `.ssproj` file and click `Open`.
* Or select `File` > `Open Recent` to pick a project you have opened or saved before.
* Or drag the `.ssproj` file into the Editor window.
* If you have installed SuperSplat as an app, double-click the `.ssproj` file in File Explorer (Windows) or Finder (macOS).

SuperSplat restores the project to its last saved state.

If the browser blocks reading the file you picked, SuperSplat shows a **File Access Blocked** message; click **OK** and choose the file again in the browser's file dialog. A project opened this way keeps its name, but **Save** asks where to write it, as it does in browsers without the File System Access API.

## File Structure

The `.ssproj` format is actually a ZIP archive containing:

* A JSON document that stores the project metadata: camera, view settings, camera poses, timeline, and the list of splats.
* The splat data, stored once as uncompressed `.ply` files, plus a small per-splat file holding each splat's editing state (selection, locked and deleted Gaussians, transform, and color grades). Each splat appears as a row in the Scene Manager on load.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Managing Splats

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/scene-management/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/scene-management.md

The **Scene Manager** lists the splats in the current project. Each splat file you import appears as a separate row. This makes it possible to assemble several captures, compare revisions, or align independently captured areas before exporting them together.

[Image: The Scene Manager listing two splats, with the Transform and Colors sections below]

## The Active Splat

Click a row to make that splat active. The active splat is the target for:

- Gaussian selection and editing
- The **Transform** and **Colors** sections of the Scene Manager, and the **Splat Data** panel
- Camera focus and measurement tools

Only one splat can be active at a time. Selecting a row does not change its visibility.

## Transform and Colors

Below the splat list, the **Transform** section shows the active splat's **Position**, **Rotation**, and **Scale** for precise numeric edits (see [Transform, Measure and Align](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md)). The **Colors** section below it grades the color of the active splat, or of the selected Gaussians, and bakes the result with **Apply** (see [Color and Appearance](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/color-and-appearance.md#colors)). Click a section's header to collapse or expand it; **Transform** starts expanded and **Colors** collapsed.

Right-click a section header to copy or paste all of its values, or right-click a row to copy or paste one value. Values travel through the system clipboard as plain JSON text, which makes it easy to give several splats the same transform or color grade.

## Add Splats

Use **File > Import** (or **File > Import Recent** for a file you have loaded before), the import button in the Scene Manager header, or drag supported files into the viewport. Importing adds splats to the current project; it does not replace splats that are already loaded. When you pick or drop a mixed set of files, the **Import Files** dialog lets you choose which of them to import (see [Importing Several Files](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/import-export.md#importing-several-files)).

**File > New** is different: it starts a new, empty project after asking for confirmation if the current project contains data.

See [Import and Export](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/import-export.md) for supported formats and multi-file import requirements.

## Visibility and Solo Mode

Click the eye icon on a splat row to show or hide it. Hidden splats are excluded from splat exports, so check visibility before exporting a combined result.

Use the **Solo** button in the Scene Manager header when you want to work on one splat without changing your visibility setup:

1. Select a splat.
2. Enable **Solo** to hide every other splat.
3. Select another row to switch which splat is shown.
4. Disable **Solo** to restore the visibility state that existed before Solo mode was enabled.

If you import a splat while Solo mode is active, select its row to view it.

## Rename and Remove Splats

Double-click a splat name to rename it. Renaming can be undone and redone.

Click the trash icon on a splat row to remove the entire splat from the project. Removing a splat cannot be undone. This is different from deleting selected Gaussians, which is recorded in the edit history and can be undone. Save an `.ssproj` copy first if you may need the splat later.

## Assemble Multiple Captures

A typical multi-splat workflow is:

1. Import all captures.
2. Use Solo mode to inspect and clean each splat independently.
3. Use the [transform tools](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md) to position, rotate and scale each splat.
4. Show the splats together and check their alignment from several camera angles.
5. Hide any splat that should not be included.
6. Choose **File > Export > PLY** to combine the visible splats into one PLY file.

Saving with **File > Save** creates an editable `.ssproj` project instead of a merged PLY. See [Managing Projects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/managing-projects.md).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Selection and Cleanup

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md

Select a splat in the **Scene Manager** before editing it. Gaussian selection and cleanup operations apply only to that active splat, even when several splats are visible.

## Selection Mode and X-Ray

The [mode strip](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#mode-strip) beside the View Cube controls how the 2D selection tools decide which Gaussians they hit, and shows you what a drag would select.

| Control | Shortcut | Setting | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Centers** / **Rings** | <kbd>M</kbd> | **Centers** (default) | Selects by center: a Gaussian is picked when its center point falls inside the tool's shape. A dot marks each Gaussian center. |
| | | **Rings** | Selects by footprint: a Gaussian is picked when any part of its projected ellipse falls inside the shape, so large, soft Gaussians at the edge of a selection are included. A ring outlines each footprint. |
| **X-Ray** | <kbd>N</kbd> | On (default) | Selects through the whole scene: every Gaussian under the tool's shape is picked, regardless of what is in front of it. |
| | | Off | Selects only the visible surface: Gaussians hidden behind others are left alone. Turn X-Ray off to clean the surface of a scene without punching through it. |

The mode, Markers, and X-Ray settings are remembered between sessions.

[Image: Gaussian centers shown in Centers mode]

[Image: Gaussian rings shown in Rings mode]

### Markers

The center dots and rings are called markers. Press <kbd>Tab</kbd> (or click **Markers** on the mode strip) to show or hide them on the unselected Gaussians. Markers are off by default, so you see the plain rendered splat; switching mode turns them on. Hiding the markers does not change how selection works, and selected Gaussians keep their indicators: a dot or ring in the selection color (yellow by default).

A marker's color shows its selection state. Selected markers always use the selection color. Unselected center dots use the unselected color (blue by default), while unselected rings take the colors of their Gaussians. With X-Ray off, unselected markers are drawn only on the Gaussians a selection could reach from the current view, so you can see what a drag would pick before you make it. Selected markers are always drawn. Marker size, colors, and the selection tint and outline are set from the mode strip's press-and-hold menus; see [Markers and Selection Display](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/color-and-appearance.md#appearance).

Locked and deleted Gaussians cannot be selected. Fully transparent Gaussians can, which makes it possible to clean up invisible leftovers that still cost memory and rendering time.

## Selection Tools

Each Scene Manager row represents an imported splat, while the selection tools act on individual Gaussians within the active splat. Use these tools to crop a splat or remove unwanted Gaussians:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| [Image: Rectangle Selection] **Rectangle Selection** (<kbd>R</kbd>) | Click to select a single Gaussian, or click and drag to select everything inside a rectangle. This is the default selection tool. |
| [Image: Brush Selection] **Brush Selection** (<kbd>B</kbd>) | Click and drag to paint a selection with a circular brush. Adjust the brush size with the <kbd>[</kbd> (decrease) and <kbd>]</kbd> (increase) keys, or with <kbd>Alt</kbd> + mouse wheel. Ideal for organic selection work. |
| [Image: Polygon Selection] **Polygon Selection** (<kbd>P</kbd>) | Click to place the vertices of a polygon. Press <kbd>Backspace</kbd> to remove the last placed point. Close the shape by clicking the first point, double-clicking, or pressing <kbd>Enter</kbd>. Useful for precise selections with straight edges. Shares a toolbar button with Lasso Selection. |
| [Image: Lasso Selection] **Lasso Selection** (<kbd>L</kbd>) | Click and drag to draw a freeform shape. Gaussians within the outline are selected. Shares a toolbar button with Polygon Selection. |
| [Image: Eyedropper Selection] **Eyedropper Selection** (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd>) | Click the viewport to select Gaussians of a similar color. A threshold slider (0–1) controls the sensitivity of the color match. Shares a toolbar button with Flood Selection. |
| [Image: Flood Selection] **Flood Selection** (<kbd>O</kbd>) | Click the viewport to grow a 2D selection from that point with a flood fill. A threshold slider (0–1) controls its sensitivity. Particularly useful for isolated stray Gaussians (floaters). Shares a toolbar button with Eyedropper Selection. |
| [Image: Sphere Brush Selection] **Sphere Brush Selection** (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd>) | Paint a selection in 3D. Each point of the stroke is projected onto the surface under the cursor and selects the Gaussians inside a sphere there, so the brush follows the surface instead of selecting through the scene. The brush size is shared with Brush Selection (<kbd>[</kbd>, <kbd>]</kbd>, <kbd>Alt</kbd> + mouse wheel) and maps to a world-space radius at the picked depth. |
| [Image: Sphere Selection] **Sphere Selection** | Creates a 3D spherical volume for volumetric selection. Double-click anywhere in the scene to position the sphere center. Move and Scale buttons in the toolbar (or the <kbd>1</kbd> and <kbd>3</kbd> keys) switch the sphere's gizmo — dragging the scale gizmo's center handle changes the radius — or enter its **Position** (X, Y, Z) and **Radius** numerically. Click **Set**, **Add**, **Remove**, or **Intersect** to apply the volume to the current selection. |
| [Image: Box Selection] **Box Selection** | Creates a 3D box for volumetric selection. Double-click anywhere in the scene to position the box center. Move, Rotate, and Scale buttons in the toolbar (or the <kbd>1</kbd>, <kbd>2</kbd>, and <kbd>3</kbd> keys) switch the box's gizmo, so the box can be freely positioned, rotated, and resized — or enter its **Position** (X, Y, Z) and **Size** (X, Y, Z) numerically. While the rotate gizmo is active, the **Size** fields are replaced by **Rotation** fields (enter `0, 0, 0` to reset the orientation). Click **Set**, **Add**, **Remove**, or **Intersect** to apply the volume to the current selection. Ideal for selecting Gaussians within a specific region of 3D space. |

Two of the toolbar buttons hold a pair of tools: **Polygon** / **Lasso** and **Eyedropper** / **Flood**. Click the button to activate the tool it currently shows, or press and hold it to choose the other; the button then remembers your choice. The keyboard shortcuts always activate a specific tool.

[Image: The bottom toolbar with the Polygon / Lasso popup open]

### Selection Modifiers

The 2D selection tools and the Sphere Brush support modifier keys to control how the selection is applied:

| Modifier | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **None** | Replace the current selection with the new selection |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> | Add to the current selection |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> | Remove from the current selection |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> | Keep only Gaussians that are in both the current selection and the new selection |

While one of these tools is active, the cursor shows which operation the current modifier keys will apply. A plain crosshair means **Set**; a badge on the crosshair indicates **Add** (`+`), **Remove** (`−`), or **Intersect** (`∩`). The same feedback appears when selecting a value range in the [Splat Data panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/data-panel.md).

The 3D volume tools (Sphere Selection and Box Selection) have **Set**, **Add**, **Remove**, and **Intersect** buttons in their toolbar instead of using modifier keys. Their volumes are transformed with the same gizmos as the transform tools: clicking the active gizmo mode button again hides the gizmo, the gizmo follows the local/world coordinate-space toggle, and volume edits are undoable while the tool is active. Press <kbd>F</kbd> to frame the volume in the viewport.

## Lock, Delete, and Restore

Use **Select > Lock Selection** or press <kbd>H</kbd> to lock the selected Gaussians. Locking clears the selection and prevents those Gaussians from being selected or deleted. This is useful for protecting a finished area while you clean nearby geometry. Choose **Select > Unlock All** or press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd> to unlock all locked Gaussians in the active splat.

Delete selected Gaussians with **Select > Delete Selection**, <kbd>Delete</kbd>, or <kbd>Backspace</kbd>. Deletion is non-destructive while you edit: use Undo to reverse the latest deletion, or choose **Select > Reset Splat** to restore all deleted Gaussians in the active splat. Reset Splat does not unlock locked Gaussians.

Lock, unlock, delete, and reset operations are recorded in the edit history. Removing an entire row from the Scene Manager is different and cannot be undone.

## Duplicate and Separate a Selection

When a Gaussian selection exists, the **Edit** menu provides two ways to turn it into another splat:

- **Duplicate** copies the selected Gaussians into a new splat and keeps the originals unchanged.
- **Separate** creates a new splat from the selected Gaussians and deletes them from the original splat.

Both operations can be undone and are useful for giving one region its own transform or visibility.

## Cleanup Recipes

### Remove Floaters

1. Turn off **X-Ray** (<kbd>N</kbd>) so selections stop at the visible surface, and press <kbd>Tab</kbd> if you want to see the markers while you work.
2. Use Flood Selection for an isolated patch, or Lasso, Brush, Sphere Brush, Sphere, or Box Selection for a larger region.
3. Rotate the camera and add to or remove from the selection until the intended geometry is isolated.
4. Press <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd>.
5. Inspect the result from several angles and use Undo if too much was removed.

### Crop a Splat

1. Select the region you want to keep with Box, Sphere, Lasso, or Polygon Selection. Leave **X-Ray** on so the selection reaches through the whole scene.
2. Choose **Select > Invert**.
3. Delete the inverted selection.
4. Export the cleaned result, or save an `.ssproj` if you want to preserve the splat and project setup.

### Protect Finished Areas

Select a finished region and press <kbd>H</kbd> to lock it. Continue cleaning the remaining selectable Gaussians, then press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd> when you need to edit the protected region again.

For attribute-driven cleanup, use the [Splat Data panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/data-panel.md) to select ranges such as low opacity or extreme scale values.

## Next Step

Continue to [Transform, Measure and Align](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md) to transform selected Gaussians or whole splats, calibrate scale, align captures and merge visible splats.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Transform, Measure and Align

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md

SuperSplat can transform an entire imported splat or only the Gaussians selected within it. The current selection determines which behavior is used:

| Active splat state | Transform target |
|---|---|
| No Gaussians selected | The whole active splat |
| One or more Gaussians selected | Only the selected Gaussians |

If you intended to move the whole splat, choose **Select > None** before transforming it.

## Transform Tools

Select the active splat, then choose a tool from the bottom toolbar:

- **Move** (<kbd>1</kbd>) translates the target.
- **Rotate** (<kbd>2</kbd>) rotates the target.
- **Scale** (<kbd>3</kbd>) scales the target.

Drag the gizmo handles in the viewport. For precise values, edit **Position**, **Rotation**, and uniform **Scale** in the **Transform** section below the Scene Manager's splat list (click its header to collapse or expand it). Transform operations can be undone and redone.

[Image: The Move tool's gizmo on the active splat, with the splat's values in the Transform section]

### Copy and Paste a Transform

Right-click the **Transform** header and choose **Copy** to copy the whole transform, or right-click the **Position**, **Rotation**, or **Scale** row to copy just that value. Values are copied at full precision as plain JSON text, for example `{"position":[1.5,0,-2],"rotation":[0,90,0],"scale":1}`, so they can be pasted back into the Editor, into another splat, or into any text field. **Paste** on the header accepts any subset of these keys, so `{"scale":2}` changes only the scale; **Paste** on a row accepts a bare value such as `[1.5,0,-2]` or a copied section. A paste is a single undo step. Invalid clipboard contents change nothing and briefly flash the target red.

Gizmos start in the splat's local coordinate space. Press <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> (or the coordinate-space toggle in the bottom toolbar) to switch between local and world space.

## Position the Pivot

The pivot marks the transform origin — where rotation and scale are applied — and defines the splat's local coordinate frame:

- While Move, Rotate, or Scale is active, double-click a visible surface to place the pivot at that point.
- Click **Reset Pivot** in the bottom toolbar to return the pivot to the splat's origin and reset its orientation. <kbd>Shift</kbd>-click it to place the pivot at the bound center instead: the center of the whole splat, or of the selected Gaussians when a selection exists.
- The [Orient tool](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/transform-measure-align.md#orient-a-splat-to-the-grid) can set the pivot from a plane picked on the splat's surface.

Moving the pivot does not move the splat until you use a transform control. Pivot changes are undoable, and a custom pivot is saved with the project in `.ssproj` files.

## Orient a Splat to the Grid

The Orient tool levels a mis-rotated splat — a Z-up import, a tilted capture, or an upside-down scan — by aligning a plane or a vertical line picked on its surface to the grid:

1. Activate **Orient** in the bottom toolbar.
2. Click points on the splat:
   - **Three points** on a surface that should be level, such as a floor or table top, define a plane.
   - **Two points** on an edge that should be vertical, such as a door frame or column, define a line. Click the bottom point first, then the top. Use this when the capture has no usable floor.
3. Click a placed point and use its move gizmo to refine the position. <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> removes the active point, **Clear** removes all of them, and <kbd>F</kbd> frames the points in the viewport.
4. Press **Align to Grid**.
   - With three points, the whole active splat rotates and translates so the picked plane lands exactly on the grid plane, pivoting around the picked points so the clicked region stays in place. The side of the plane facing the camera becomes up. If the result is upside down, orbit underneath the plane and press **Align to Grid** again.
   - With two points, the whole active splat rotates about the midpoint of the line so the line points straight up from the grid, from the first point to the second. Click order sets the direction, so tilted, sideways, and upside-down captures all level in one step. The splat is not moved onto the grid, because a line does not define a floor.

When the picked plane or line is within 3 degrees of one of the splat's own axes, the rotation snaps to that axis, so conventional Z-up imports produce exact quarter turns.

Alignment applies to the whole active splat regardless of any Gaussian selection and is recorded as a single undoable operation. The grid is displayed while the tool is active, even if hidden. The target is the first grid plane enabled under **Planes** in the [Overlays](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#overlays) popup: XZ by default, or XY or YZ if you have turned XZ off. With two points, "up" is the axis perpendicular to that plane: +Y for XZ, +Z for XY, and +X for YZ.

While Orient is active, the pivot button in the bottom toolbar becomes **Set Pivot**. With three points placed, it stores the picked plane as the splat's pivot and local frame instead of moving the splat: local-space gizmos and the **Transform** section then work in that frame. This is useful for transforming along a surface's own axes without rotating the splat itself.

## Align Multiple Splats

To align independently captured splats:

1. Import each capture as a separate splat.
2. Select the first splat and leave it fixed as a reference.
3. Select the splat to align and choose **Select > None** so the whole splat is the transform target.
4. Use Move, Rotate, and Scale, checking the result from more than one camera angle.
5. Toggle visibility or use Solo mode to compare the splats.

The grid uses meters, with major divisions at 1 m and minor divisions at 0.1 m. Enable **Bounding Box** and **Dimensions** in the [Overlays](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#overlays) popup when a numeric size check is useful.

## Measure and Rescale a Splat

The Measure tool reports the distance between two surface points and can rescale the whole active splat to a known real-world length.

1. Activate **Measure** in the bottom toolbar.
2. Click a surface to place the first marker, then click again to place the second.
3. Click either marker and use its move gizmo to refine the position.
4. Read the measured length in the toolbar above the bottom controls. With **Dimensions** enabled in the Overlays popup, the length is also labeled along the line in the viewport.
5. To calibrate the splat, enter the real distance in that field. SuperSplat uniformly rescales the whole active splat around the midpoint of the two markers.

<kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> removes the active marker while Measure is active, and <kbd>F</kbd> frames the placed markers. Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> to leave the tool. Changing the length is undoable.

## Merge Visible Splats

After aligning and cleaning the splats, make every splat you want to include visible and choose **File > Export > PLY**. The export combines the visible splats into one file.

**File > Save** preserves the editable splats in an `.ssproj` project; it does not create a merged PLY. See [Managing Splats](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/scene-management.md) and [Managing Projects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/managing-projects.md).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Color and Appearance

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/color-and-appearance/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/color-and-appearance.md

Two different sets of controls affect how a splat looks in SuperSplat:

- The **Colors** section of the Scene Manager changes the splat data itself: tint, temperature, saturation, brightness, tonal range, and transparency. These edits are saved and exported with the splat.
- The [mode strip](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#mode-strip) and the viewport colors in [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences) change only how the viewport draws the markers and the selection. They never modify the splat.

## Colors

Expand the **Colors** section at the bottom of the [Scene Manager](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/scene-management.md), below **Transform**, by clicking its header. The sliders hold a pending color grade that is previewed live in the viewport on the Gaussians it would affect: the current selection, or the whole active splat when nothing is selected. Click **Apply** to bake the grade into those Gaussians; the sliders then return to neutral, ready for the next adjustment. To grade one region differently from the rest, select it first.

[Image: The Colors section of the Scene Manager]

### Controls

| Control | Range | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| **Tint** | color | Multiplies the color by the chosen tint. White leaves the source color unchanged. |
| **Temperature** | −0.5 to 0.5 | Shifts the result toward cooler (negative) or warmer (positive) tones. |
| **Saturation** | 0 to 2 | Reduces or increases color intensity. `1` leaves saturation unchanged. |
| **Brightness** | −1 to 1 | Darkens or brightens. `0` leaves brightness unchanged. |
| **Black Point** | 0 to 1 | Raises the darkest value that is mapped to black, increasing shadow clipping. |
| **White Point** | 0 to 1 | Lowers the brightest value that is mapped to white, increasing highlight clipping. |
| **Transparency** | −6 to 6 | Reduces (negative) or increases (positive) opacity relative to the source values. |

Black Point always stays below White Point: moving one into the other pushes the other along. **Reset** removes any grade already applied to the targeted Gaussians and returns the sliders to neutral. Changing the selection discards a pending grade that has not been applied. Apply and Reset are recorded in the edit history and can be undone and redone.

### A Practical Correction Workflow

1. Set the viewport tone mapping and background color in [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences), so you are judging the scene in its intended viewing conditions.
2. Correct overall warmth with **Temperature**.
3. Adjust **Brightness**, then set **Black Point** and **White Point** to establish the tonal range.
4. Use **Saturation** and **Tint** for the final color balance.
5. Check the result from several camera angles. Spherical harmonic color can change with view direction.
6. Click **Apply**.

Tone mapping and the background color are view settings; the Colors section changes the splat itself.

### Copy and Paste a Grade

Right-click the **Colors** header and choose **Copy** to copy every slider value, or right-click a single row to copy just that value. The values are copied as plain JSON text, for example `{"tint":[1,1,1],"temperature":0.1,"saturation":1.2,"brightness":0,"blackPoint":0,"whitePoint":1,"transparency":0}`, so you can keep them in a note or paste them into another Editor session. **Paste** on the header accepts any subset of these keys, so `{"saturation":1.2}` changes only saturation; **Paste** on a row accepts a bare value or a copied section. **Tint** also accepts a hex color such as `#ffcc88`. Pasted values are clamped to each slider's range, and invalid clipboard contents change nothing and briefly flash the target red.

Copy and paste work on the pending grade shown in the sliders: click **Apply** after pasting to bake it in.

### Save and Export Behavior

Applied grades become part of the splat's color data, so they are stored in `.ssproj` projects and included in every export format. Click **Apply** before saving or exporting: a pending grade that has not been applied is only a preview.

## Markers and Selection Display

How the viewport draws markers and the selection is set on the [mode strip](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#mode-strip) beside the View Cube. These settings are saved with your preferences and affect only the viewport. See [Selection Mode and X-Ray](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md#selection-mode-and-x-ray) for how the mode and X-Ray change what the selection tools hit.

### Mode Options

Press and hold **Centers** or **Rings** on the mode strip to open its options. A short press just chooses the mode.

| Mode | Control | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Centers | **Center Size** | 2 | Size of the center dots in pixels (0–10). |
| | **Splat Colors** | Off | Draw unselected center dots in the colors of their Gaussians instead of the unselected color. |
| Rings | **Ring Thickness** | 4 | Thickness of the ring outlines (1–50). |
| | **Splat Colors** | On | Draw unselected rings in the colors of their Gaussians instead of the unselected color. |

Selected markers always use the selected color.

### Markers Options

Press and hold **Markers** on the mode strip to open its options. A short press toggles the markers, like <kbd>Tab</kbd>.

| Control | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Markers Only** | Off | Hide the Gaussians themselves while the markers are shown, leaving only the dots or rings. |
| **Tint Selection** | Off | Tint the selected Gaussians with the selected color. |
| **Outline Selection** | Off | Draw an outline around the silhouette of the selection in the selected color. |

### Viewport Colors

The **Background Color**, **Selected Color**, **Unselected Color**, and **Locked Color** are set in the **Colors** section of the [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences) popup. They are used by the markers, the selection tint and outline, and the [Splat Data](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/data-panel.md) histogram.

For per-Gaussian inspection and selection by color or other attributes, use the [Splat Data panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/data-panel.md). To animate the viewport camera after finishing the splat's appearance, see the [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data Panel

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/data-panel/
