## Manage

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md

The [Manage page](https://superspl.at/manage) is your splat library on superspl.at. From here you can list and search your published splats, edit metadata, toggle visibility, choose whether visitors can download the source, pick a license, delete splats, and **open any splat in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md)** to curate its viewing experience.

You must be signed in with a PlayCanvas account to access Manage. See [Account Creation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/account-management/user-accounts/account-creation.md).

[Image: The Manage page table with several splats]

## The list view

On desktop the page shows a sortable table; on mobile each splat is rendered as a card, with its actions in a menu that can also make the splat public or unlisted.

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Splat** | Thumbnail, title, and description. Click the thumbnail to open the splat's [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md). |
| **Visibility** | Dropdown for **Public** (globe icon) or **Unlisted** (link icon). |
| **Date** | Relative time the splat was uploaded; hover for the exact timestamp. |
| **Views** | View count on the public scene page. |
| **Likes** | Thumbs-up count. |
| **Size** | Human-readable file size of the published splat. |
| **Actions** | Icon buttons for **Edit details** (pencil), **Open in Studio**, and **Delete** (trash). Hover a button for its name. |

Click a column header to sort. Sortable fields are **Date** (default — newest first), **Views**, **Likes**, and **Size**. The list paginates at **25 splats per page**.

## Searching

The search bar above the table filters across **title** and **description**. The search box is hidden until you've uploaded at least one splat.

## Uploading a new splat

The **Upload Splat** button in the page header opens the Upload dialog. See [Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md) for the full flow.

## Editing splat metadata

Click **Edit details** (the pencil) in the row's **Actions** column to open the **Edit Splat** dialog.

[Image: The Edit Splat dialog]

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Title** | The headline shown on the [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) sidebar. |
| **Description** | A longer summary shown on the scene page. |
| **Software Used** | Multi-select of the tools you used to capture or train the splat. Chosen entries appear as chips on the public scene page. |
| **Visibility** | **Public** (appears in [Explore](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/explore.md) listings and searches) or **Unlisted** (reachable only via the direct URL). |
| **Downloadable** | Toggle that controls whether visitors can download the source splat from the scene page. Off by default. |
| **License** | Shown when **Downloadable** is on. Pick the [Creative Commons license](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md#downloadable--license) that applies to your splat. |

The **Preview** card in the top right of the dialog shows the thumbnail, format, and download size. It also has **View** (opens the public scene page) and **Edit in Studio** (opens [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) — disabled if the splat is still processing or in an unsupported format).

### Downloadable & license

When you enable **Downloadable**, you must choose a Creative Commons license that tells visitors how they can reuse the file:

| Code | License |
|------|---------|
| `by` | Attribution |
| `by-nd` | Attribution-NoDerivatives |
| `by-sa` | Attribution-ShareAlike |
| `by-nc` | Attribution-NonCommercial |
| `by-nc-nd` | Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives |
| `by-nc-sa` | Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike |

The selected license is surfaced on the [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) Download dialog with an icon, summary, and a one-click **Copy credit** button for attribution.

## Visibility from the list

You don't need to open the Edit dialog to change visibility — use the **Visibility** dropdown in each row. The button shows the current setting (icon and label) and a chevron; choose **Public** or **Unlisted** from the menu. Unlisted splats are excluded from [Explore](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/explore.md) and won't appear when other users search.

## Deleting a splat

Click **Delete** in the row's **Actions** column. A confirmation dialog asks you to confirm.

:::danger
Deleting a splat is permanent and cannot be undone.
:::

## Opening a splat in Studio

Use **Open in Studio** in the row's **Actions** column, or **Edit in Studio** on the dialog's preview card, to launch [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) for that splat. The control is disabled while the splat is still processing or in an unsupported format, and hovering it then says **Splat is not available for editing**. Studio's URL is `superspl.at/scene/<hash>/studio`. Only the splat's owner can open Studio for it.

## See also

- [Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md) — publish a splat without going through the Editor
- [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) — curate the published viewing experience
- [Scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) — what visitors see when they open a splat

## Streaming & Performance

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md

When you [publish from the Editor](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/editor.md) or [directly upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md) a splat, SuperSplat compresses it to the **SOG** family of formats for fast delivery. Large splats are automatically converted to **Streamed SOG** so they load quickly and run smoothly on any device.

## How your splat is compressed

A published splat takes one of two forms:

- **SOG** — the splat is compressed to a single, non-streamed **`.sog`** file.
- **Streamed SOG** — SuperSplat generates a set of **levels of detail (LODs)** using [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md), halving the Gaussian count at each level (decimation), and compresses them into a **Streamed SOG** bundle: a `lod-meta.json` index plus per-LOD `.sog` chunks. Larger splats produce more levels, so expect some extra back-end processing time after upload.

Which one you get depends on how you publish:

- **From the Editor**, the **Generate LODs** toggle in the [Publish Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/editor.md) dialog decides. It's on by default for scenes of 1 million Gaussians or more that span a large area. Scenes of more than 40 million Gaussians must be streamed, so for them the toggle is switched on and can't be turned off.
- **With [Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md)**, a PLY or SPZ file gets an **Auto generate LODs** checkbox, ticked automatically at 1 million Gaussians or more; you can override it before publishing, except above 40 million Gaussians, where it is locked on. A SOG file is published as a single file, and splats uploaded as a pre-built LCC or SSOG archive are always streamed.

## Near-instant loads and the Gaussian budget

A Streamed SOG splat loads **progressively**: the viewer shows the scene as soon as the lowest level of detail is ready, then fills in finer detail as it streams in. This gives near-instant time-to-first-frame even for very large scenes. The loading bar tracks the streamed files, and any [collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md) data keeps loading in the background after the scene appears.

At runtime the viewer enforces a **Gaussian budget** — a cap on how many Gaussians are drawn at once — so the scene stays within a sensible amount of memory and renders at a good frame rate. Visitors choose the budget with the **Quality** slider in the viewer's [settings panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#the-settings-panel), from a ladder for their device:

| Device | Performance | Default | High | Max |
|--------|-------------|---------|------|-----|
| Desktop | 2M | 4M | 8M | 16M |
| Phones, tablets and headsets | 1M | 2M | 4M | 8M |
| Meta Quest and Pico, during a VR or AR session | 0.5M | 1M | 2M | — |

Phones and tablets start at **Performance** and other devices at **Default**; the viewer remembers the visitor's choice. Positions the device doesn't have the memory for are disabled. At **Performance**, the viewer also renders at half resolution (0.8× in a Meta Quest or Pico session), unless **Performance Mode** is on. When you host the viewer yourself, the `budget` [URL parameter](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters) sets the budget for every position.

As the camera moves, the viewer raises and lowers the level of detail across the scene to stay within this budget — so you get consistent performance and bounded memory use on everything from a phone to a desktop. In a VR or AR session, detail is chosen by distance alone, so turning your head doesn't stream new detail.

To see it at work, turn on the viewer's `colorize` [URL parameter](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters), which tints each level of detail its own color:

[Image: The same view of a streamed scene, as normal on the left and with colorize on the right, where each color is a level of detail]

A splat that isn't streamed is drawn in full whatever the budget; for it, the Quality slider only changes the resolution at **Performance**.

## Bringing your own LODs

Advanced users can skip the automatic step and supply a pre-built Streamed SOG bundle:

- Generate one with the [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) CLI (use `--decimate` to build the LOD levels), then [directly upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md) the resulting bundle.
- Or build one in your browser with the [Streamed SOG](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/convert.md#streamed-sog) tab of Convert, then upload its zip.

## See also

- [Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md) — upload a ready-made splat
- [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) — generate Streamed SOG bundles yourself
- [Streamed SOG (developer guide)](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/gaussian-splatting/building/lod-streaming.md) — using Streamed SOG in your own PlayCanvas apps

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## SuperSplat Studio

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md

**SuperSplat Studio** is where you curate the viewing experience of a splat you've already [published](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/editor.md) or [directly uploaded](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md). It opens on top of the published scene and shapes what a visitor sees on its [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md): the background or skybox, tonemapping, the starting camera, a camera animation, collision geometry for walkable scenes, post effects, and on-scene annotations.

Studio writes its output as a single JSON document, the [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md), which the open-source [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) reads at runtime.

[Image: The Studio window: the Scene tab on the left, the viewport, and the timeline open along the bottom]

## Launching Studio

Studio runs at **`https://superspl.at/scene/<hash>/studio`**. Only the splat's owner can open it; for anyone else the URL 404s.

There are three ways to get there:

- On the [Manage page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md), click **Open in Studio** in the splat's row.
- In a splat's **Edit Splat** dialog on the Manage page, click **Edit in Studio** in the preview card.
- On your own splat's [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md), use the **Edit in Studio** entry point.

:::note Desktop recommended

Studio is built for a desktop browser with a keyboard and mouse. On a phone or tablet you'll see a "Studio works best on desktop" warning when you open it. You can continue, but expect a constrained UI.

:::

## The layout

- **Header**: **Back to manage**, the scene name, and on the right **Timeline**, **Import**, **Export**, **View** and **Save**. See [Saving changes](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md#saving-changes).
- **Left panel**, with two tabs:
  - **Scene**: the sections that make up the scene's look and behavior, from top to bottom:
    - [Look & Tone](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md): background color, skybox, tonemapping, High Precision Rendering and anti-aliasing.
    - [Cameras](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md): the starting camera and the field of view.
    - [Animation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md#playing-on-open): whether the camera animation plays when the scene opens.
    - [Collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md): voxel geometry that makes a scene walkable.
    - [Post Effects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects.md): sharpness, bloom, color grading, vignette and chromatic fringing.
  - **Annotations**: the list of on-scene [annotations](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md).
- **Viewport**: a live preview of how visitors will see the scene, with a toolbar along the bottom.
- **Timeline**: a panel along the bottom for keyframing the [camera animation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md). It is hidden until you click **Timeline** or press <kbd>T</kbd>.

### The viewport toolbar

| Button | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Undo** / **Redo** | Step through your edits. |
| **Move** | The default tool: navigate and select. |
| **Add annotation** | Place an [annotation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md#adding-an-annotation) by clicking the splat (<kbd>C</kbd>). |
| **Orbit mode** / **Fly mode** | Switch how the viewport camera moves. |
| **Frame selection** | Frame the selection in the viewport (<kbd>F</kbd>). |
| **Reset camera** | Return the viewport camera to its starting view (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd>). |
| **Open shortcut guide** | List Studio's keyboard shortcuts. |

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> | Move, in fly mode |
| <kbd>Q</kbd> / <kbd>E</kbd> | Move down / up, in fly mode |
| Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> | Move faster / slower, in fly mode |
| Double-click | Set the orbit point |
| <kbd>F</kbd> | Frame the selection |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd> | Reset the camera |
| <kbd>C</kbd> | Add an annotation |
| <kbd>T</kbd> | Show or hide the timeline |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play or pause the camera animation |
| <kbd>Enter</kbd> | Add a keyframe at the playhead |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> | Undo / redo (<kbd>Cmd</kbd> on macOS) |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Cancel or deselect |

## Saving changes

Edits are not saved automatically. **Save** is enabled while you have unsaved changes, and it writes your complete Experience Settings to superspl.at. Visitors who open the scene page from then on see the new version. If you try to leave Studio with unsaved changes, it asks you to confirm before they're lost.

Skybox and collision files are the exception: they upload as soon as you add them, without **Save**.

The other header buttons work with the settings as a file:

- **Export** downloads the current settings as `settings-<hash>.json`, for example to use with a [viewer you host yourself](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md).
- **Import** replaces the current settings with a JSON file you choose, after asking for confirmation. Click **Save** to publish them.
- **View** opens the scene page.

Studio also reads settings saved in older versions of the format. See [Schema versioning](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md#schema-versioning).

## AI agents

In a browser that supports the experimental [WebMCP API](https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/), Studio registers tools that let an AI agent work in your open Studio tab, much like the Editor's [AI Agents (WebMCP)](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/webmcp.md) tools. An agent can read the scene and the live camera, pick points on the splat, capture the viewport as an image, create and update cameras and annotations, edit the camera animation, and play or seek the timeline. Its edits share your undo history.

Agents can't save: you review what an agent did and click **Save** yourself.

## See also

- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract Studio writes and the Viewer reads
- [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) — how visitors navigate the scene you curate
- [Scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) — what visitors see after Studio changes are saved

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Look & Tone

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md

The **Look & Tone** section, at the top of the **Scene** tab in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md), sets what surrounds your splat and how the whole image is rendered. Changes show in the viewport straight away.

[Image: The Look & Tone section]

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Background** | The solid color behind the splat. Click the swatch to open a color picker. |
| **Skybox** | **Upload** an equirectangular image to surround the splat, or delete the current one. See [Skybox](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md#skybox). |
| **Tonemapping** | How the renderer maps high-dynamic-range output to the display. See [Tonemapping](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md#tonemapping). |
| **High Precision Rendering** | Renders with more precision, at the cost of more GPU work per frame. Use it when bright highlights, fine grading or post effects show banding. [Bloom](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects.md#bloom) needs it. Off by default. |
| **Anti-aliasing** | Draws the splat for anti-aliased training, such as Mip-Splatting. On by default. Turn it off if small or distant Gaussians look too faint. See [Anti-aliasing](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md#anti-aliasing). |

## Skybox

Click **Upload** next to **Skybox** to open the **Upload Skybox** dialog. It takes one `.webp` or `.hdr` file. HDR files are converted in your browser before they upload. For best results, use an **equirectangular** image: a 2:1 panoramic projection that maps cleanly onto the surrounding sphere.

Each scene can have one skybox, and uploading another replaces it. The upload happens immediately and doesn't need **Save**. The trash icon deletes the skybox.

The background color still matters with a skybox: it shows anywhere the skybox doesn't cover.

### When to use one or the other

- **Background color only** — for studio-style presentations where you want the focus on the splat itself.
- **Skybox** — for scenes captured outdoors or in believable environments, where matching the surrounding lighting and horizon matters.

## Tonemapping

| Option | Notes |
|--------|-------|
| **None** | Pass-through with no scaling. |
| **Linear** | No tonemapping curve: output is linear. |
| **Filmic** | Classic film-emulating curve. |
| **Hejl** | Hejl-Burgess-Dawson curve. |
| **ACES** | ACES filmic curve. |
| **ACES 2** | ACES variant with rolled-off highlights. |
| **Neutral** | Khronos Neutral tonemap. |

## Anti-aliasing

Splats trained with anti-aliasing, such as with Mip-Splatting, draw too bright without compensation. Studio's switch turns that compensation on (the default) or off for the whole scene, and saves the choice with the scene's settings. On superspl.at, scene pages and embeds follow the switch: compensation is on unless you turn it off here.

## In the viewer

- **AR** — the skybox and background color are hidden during an [AR session](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md), so the room shows through around the splat. VR sessions keep them.
- **Self-hosting** — the viewer doesn't load the skybox or the anti-aliasing setting from the scene's settings. When you [host the viewer yourself](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters), pass the image with the `skybox` URL parameter or the `skyboxUrl` option, override High Precision Rendering with `hpr`, and set anti-aliasing with `aa`. Without `aa`, each splat file's own anti-aliasing tag decides.

## See also

- [Post Effects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects.md) — sharpness, bloom, color grading, vignette and chromatic fringing
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract that stores these settings

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Cameras

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md

The **Cameras** section — in the **Scene** tab of [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md)'s left panel — defines the **starting camera** for your published splat: the view a visitor lands on when they open your [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) (unless the scene [plays its camera animation on open](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md#playing-on-open) instead). The camera has a **position**, a **target** (the point it looks at), and a **field of view**.

[Image: The Cameras section with Camera 1 and its Lens settings]

:::note

Studio currently supports a single camera. Support for multiple cameras is coming.

:::

## Setting the camera

The camera is listed as **Camera 1** with three icon buttons:

- **Go to camera** — flies the viewport to the camera's saved pose.
- **Set camera to current view** — stores the viewport's current position, target and field of view as the starting pose in one click.
- **Edit camera** (pencil) — opens [camera edit mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md#edit-camera-mode) to frame a new starting view. The pencil turns yellow while edit mode is active.

You set the camera's **position** and **target** by framing the viewport. There are no numeric position or target inputs in the Cameras section.

### Edit camera mode

1. Click **Edit** (the pencil) in the Cameras panel. Studio enters camera edit mode: the viewport flies to the camera's saved pose, a thick yellow border frames the viewport, and a **Camera Edit Mode** badge appears at the top left, with **Apply** and **Cancel** buttons beside it.
2. Orbit, pan, and zoom the viewport to frame the shot (see [Camera Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md) for navigation).
3. Click **Apply** to save the viewport's **position**, **target** (look-at point), and **field of view** as Camera 1's stored start pose, then exit edit mode.
4. Click **Cancel** to exit without saving; the viewport returns to the last saved pose.

:::tip

While framing, **double-click a point on the splat** to set it as the focal point — the point the camera orbits around. The view smoothly re-centres on that point without moving the camera's position. Double-clicking empty space has no effect.

:::

Click **Edit** again (or press <kbd>Esc</kbd>) to exit edit mode without saving. Unlike **Cancel**, the viewport is not restored — only the stored pose stays unchanged.

[Video](https://developer.playcanvas.com/video/supersplat-studio-edit-camera.mp4)

## Lens (field of view)

Below the camera list, the **Lens** control sets the **Field of view** with a slider and a numeric input, in whole degrees from **10°** to **120°** (default **75°**). The value is the **full** viewing angle, not a half-angle. On a **wide** viewport the angle is measured **horizontally** (left to right); on a **tall** viewport it is measured **vertically** (top to bottom). You store one number — Studio and the published scene page apply it to whichever axis suits the screen shape.

This is a single, global setting: as its tooltip says, it applies to the start camera and all annotation cameras.

## Defaults

A fresh scene starts with a single camera at a **75°** field of view, with position and target chosen for the scene type:

- **Environment-style** scenes — position `[0, 2, 0]`, target `[2, 2, 0]`.
- **Object-style** scenes — position `[2, 2, -2]`, target `[0, 0, 0]`.

Frame the viewport and click **Set camera to current view**, or use [camera edit mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md#edit-camera-mode) and click **Apply**, to capture a new pose, then adjust the **Lens** field of view so the scene looks the way you want visitors to see it on first load.

## How cameras are used

- **Initial framing** — the first camera in the list is the default starting view when a visitor opens the scene page (`startMode: 'default'`). From there the viewer plays a slow, looping camera motion until the visitor takes over: an orbit around the target when the camera starts outside the splat (an object), or a gentle figure-eight when it starts inside (a scene). A [camera animation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md) replaces that motion when **Play animation on open** is on.
- **Object or scene** — whether the camera starts outside or inside the splat's bounds also decides the viewer's starting [camera mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#camera-modes) (orbit for an object, walk or fly for a scene) and how the splat is presented in [VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#scenes-and-objects).
- **Annotation poses** — each [annotation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md) embeds its own camera pose that the viewer animates to when the annotation is selected. The annotation's pose is independent of the entries in the Cameras list.

## See also

- [Camera Animation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md) — keyframed camera motion on Studio's timeline
- [Annotations](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md) — 3D-positioned hotspots that can adopt a camera pose
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract that stores the camera list

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Camera Animation

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md

A **camera animation** moves the camera along a keyframed path, from a gentle turntable around an object to a full flythrough of a captured space. In [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) you author it on the **Timeline** panel and control it from the **Animation** section of the **Scene** tab. Visitors watch it on the [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md), and can pause it or take over the camera at any time.

A scene has one camera animation. If you published the splat from the Editor with an animation from its [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md), Studio opens with that animation, ready to edit.

[Image: The timeline panel, with one keyframe selected and the playhead on it]

## The timeline panel

Click **Timeline** in the header, or press <kbd>T</kbd>, to show or hide the panel along the bottom of Studio.

| Control | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Previous keyframe** / **Next keyframe** | Jump the playhead to the neighboring keyframe. |
| **Step back one frame** / **Step forward one frame** | Move the playhead one frame. |
| **Play** / **Pause** | Play the animation in the viewport (<kbd>Space</kbd>). Unavailable in [camera edit mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md#edit-camera-mode). |
| **Add keyframe at playhead** | Store the viewport camera as a keyframe at the playhead (<kbd>Enter</kbd>). |
| **Delete selected keyframes** | Remove the selected keyframes. The count of selected keyframes is shown beside it. |
| Frame readout | The playhead's frame and the total number of frames. |
| **Duration** | Length of the animation, in seconds (0.1 to 600). |
| **FPS** | Frames per second of the timeline (1 to 120). The animation has **Duration** × **FPS** frames. |
| **Loop mode** | **Play once**, **Loop** (the default) or **Ping-pong**: play forwards, then backwards, repeatedly. |
| **Smooth** | Smoothness of the path between keyframes, from `0` (straight lines) to `1` (the default, smooth curves). |
| **Hide timeline** | Close the panel. |

Below the controls, the **Camera** track shows a ruler with a keyframe marker for every keyframe. Click or drag along the ruler to move the playhead. The trash icon on the track, **Delete camera animation**, removes the animation with all its keyframes.

## Creating keyframes

1. Open the timeline and move the playhead to the frame you want.
2. Frame the shot in the viewport.
3. Click **Add keyframe at playhead**, or press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. A keyframe that already exists at that frame is replaced.
4. Move the playhead and repeat.

Each keyframe stores the camera's position, target and field of view. Adding the first keyframe also turns on **Play animation on open**.

## Editing keyframes

- **Select** a keyframe by clicking it. <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>-click (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>-click on macOS) adds or removes keyframes from the selection, and dragging across an empty part of the track selects every keyframe it covers.
- **Move** keyframes by dragging the selection along the track.
- **Copy** keyframes by holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> while you drag.
- **Change** a keyframe by moving the playhead to it, framing the new shot and adding a keyframe again.

Every timeline edit can be undone with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> on macOS).

:::tip Smooth loops

With **Loop mode** set to **Loop**, the camera travels from the last keyframe back to the first over the remaining frames. Leave some frames after the last keyframe, and don't key both the first and last frame, or the loop will snap.

:::

## Playing on open

The **Animation** section of the **Scene** tab has one switch, **Play animation on open**:

- **On**: the scene page plays the animation as soon as it opens. Visitors can pause it or take over the camera.
- **Off**: the scene opens at the [starting camera](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md), and the animation isn't played.

If the animation has keyframes while the switch is off, the timeline shows **Viewer won't play this animation**, with a **Play on open** button that turns the switch on.

When you click **Save**, an animation without keyframes isn't saved, and the scene opens at the starting camera.

## Animating in the Editor or in Studio

You can also keyframe the camera on the Editor's [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md) and publish the animation with the splat. Both edit the same animation, so the last one saved wins: republishing from the Editor with **Override Animation** replaces what you made in Studio. Studio is the quicker route for a splat that is already published, since you see the result in the published viewer straight away.

## See also

- [Cameras](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md) — the starting camera and field of view
- [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) — how visitors play, pause and scrub an animation
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the `animTracks` and `startMode` fields this page edits

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Collision

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md

By default, splats in the viewer have no physical presence — the camera flies right through them. The **Collision** section in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) attaches a **voxel** representation of the scene to your splat so the viewer can collide against it. With collision attached, your splat becomes **walkable** — visitors can navigate it on foot rather than only orbiting or flying around it. The [Explore](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/explore.md) page also surfaces walkable scenes via its `walkable` feature filter.

:::important Scale your splat to real-world units
For walkable scenes to feel right, scale your splat so that **one unit equals one meter** before adding collision. In walk mode the viewer holds the camera at an eye height of **1.5 m** above the floor, so if your scene isn't at real-world scale, it will feel too large or too small to move around in. The viewer also offers walk mode only when the scene is at least **5 m** across in both horizontal directions.
:::

## What is voxel collision?

A voxel collision asset is a coarse, low-resolution box-based reconstruction of the splat — the surfaces visitors can stand on, lean against, or be stopped by. It's separate from the splat itself so it can be optimized independently for runtime physics rather than visual quality.

[Image: A splat with its voxel collision shown via debug rendering]

You'll typically generate it once per scene and re-generate only if the underlying splat changes significantly.

## Generating voxel collision

The recommended way to add collision is to generate it directly in Studio. The **Collision** section of the **Scene** tab has a **Generate** button, on its **Voxels** row, that runs a server-side voxelizer against your published splat — no files to prepare or upload.

[Image: The Generate Voxel Collision dialog in Studio]

1. Open the splat in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md#launching-studio) — clicking the splat's thumbnail only *views* it, so use **Open in Studio** (from Manage) or **Edit in Studio** (from the scene page). The **Collision** section is on the **Scene** tab of the left panel, below **Animation**.
2. Click **Generate** on the **Voxels** row to open the **Generate Voxel Collision** dialog.
3. Choose a **Scene type** — **Indoor**, **Outdoor** (the default), or **Object**. This tunes the voxelizer for the kind of space you're reconstructing.
4. Set the **Seed position** (**X**, **Y**, **Z**). This is the point the voxelizer flood-fills outward from to find the navigable space, so it should sit somewhere a visitor could stand. The fields are pre-filled with your current viewport camera position — frame the scene where you want before opening the dialog, or type coordinates in by hand.
5. Click **Generate**.

Generation runs on the server and usually takes a few minutes. The Collision section shows **Generation in progress. Reload to refresh status.** while it runs — Studio doesn't poll, so reload the page to pick up the result. Once it completes, the `scene.voxel.json` and `scene.voxel.bin` files are listed in the section, with their sizes and download links, and the scene becomes walkable on the next viewer reload. If generation fails, the section shows **Generation failed.**

If collision already exists, the dialog's button reads **Regenerate**, and replaces it. The trash icon, **Delete collision**, removes the current voxel asset.

:::note Voxel size
The generator uses a default voxel size of **5 cm** (`0.05` units), which is a good fit for most scenes. To use a different voxel size, generate your collision with [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) and upload the result — see [Uploading custom voxel collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md#uploading-custom-voxel-collision) below.
:::

## Uploading custom voxel collision

Uploading is the option to reach for when you want **custom collision** — for example, when the **Generate** button doesn't produce exactly what you want and you've authored or tuned the voxel files yourself. You can produce a compatible pair with the [Convert](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/convert.md) utility in the browser, or the [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) CLI for scripted or batch workflows.

1. In the **Collision** section of the **Scene** tab, click **Upload** on the **Voxels** row to open the **Upload Voxel Collision Pair** dialog.
2. Drop in (or click to choose) the pair of files that describe the collision — a `.voxel.json` file plus its `.voxel.bin` companion. You can add them together or in two steps.
3. Click **Upload Voxel Pair**. If collision already exists, the button reads **Upload Override** and replaces it.

Upload happens immediately, and the scene becomes walkable on the next viewer reload.

## Collision in the viewer

- **Loading** — the viewer shows the scene without waiting for its collision data, which is often larger than the splat. Walk mode becomes available once the data arrives.
- **Walk mode** — a **Walk Mode** button joins the toolbar, and walk becomes the scene's default camera mode. See [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#camera-modes).
- **Show Collision** — visitors can draw the voxels over the splat with **Show Collision** in the viewer's settings panel, or by pressing <kbd>V</kbd>. The overlay needs WebGPU.
- **VR** — in a VR session, visitors teleport onto the collision: only spots where someone could stand are valid targets. See [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#moving-around-in-vr).

When you [host the viewer yourself](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters), pass collision with the `collision` URL parameter: a `.voxel.json` file with its `.voxel.bin` beside it, or a `.glb` mesh.

## See also

- [Convert](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/convert.md) — generate voxel collision in the browser
- [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) — generate voxel collision in a script or build pipeline
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract that stores scene-asset references

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Post Effects

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects.md

The **Post Effects** section, at the bottom of the **Scene** tab in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md), controls the look of your scene after the splat is rendered. Effects are evaluated per frame in the viewer. Each effect has a switch that turns it on and shows its parameters.

Tonemapping and High Precision Rendering, which shape the whole image, are in the [Look & Tone](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md) section.

[Image: The Post Effects section with Bloom, Color Grading and Vignette on]

## Sharpness

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Amount** | Strength of the sharpening filter. |

Good for recovering perceived detail on dense splat captures.

## Bloom

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Intensity** | How strong the bloom glow appears. |
| **Blur Level** | Size of the bloom kernel. Larger values produce a softer, broader glow. |

Adds a glow to bright regions of the scene. Bloom needs [High Precision Rendering](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md): while it's off, the section says **Bloom requires High Precision Rendering**, and **Enable** turns it on.

## Color Grading

Color grading applies a global transform to the image.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Brightness** | Overall brightness lift. |
| **Contrast** | Tone separation between dark and light. |
| **Saturation** | Color intensity (`0` is grayscale). |
| **Tint** | An RGB color blended into the image, useful for warm or cool grades. |

## Vignette

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Intensity** | Strength of the corner darkening. |
| **Inner** | Radius at which the vignette starts. |
| **Outer** | Radius at which the vignette reaches full strength. |
| **Curvature** | Shape of the vignette falloff. |

## Chromatic Fringing

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Intensity** | Strength of the chromatic aberration effect at frame edges. |

## In the viewer

- **VR and AR** — post effects and High Precision Rendering aren't applied during a [VR or AR session](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md). The scene's tonemapping still is, and everything returns when the session ends.
- **Self-hosting** — when you [host the viewer yourself](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters), the `nofx` URL parameter turns post effects off.

## See also

- [Look & Tone](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md) — background, skybox, tonemapping and High Precision Rendering
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract that stores post-effect settings

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Annotations

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md

**Annotations** are 3D-positioned text hotspots you place on your published splat in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md). On the viewer side, each annotation shows up as a numbered hotspot visitors can click; clicking it moves the camera to a curated pose and surfaces a title and body of text. Use them to call out features, narrate a story, or give a self-guided tour of the scene.

[Image: The Annotations tab with three annotations, one selected and its card open in the viewport]

## Annotation properties

Each annotation has:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Position** | World-space `[x, y, z]` where the hotspot marker sits in the scene. |
| **Title** | Short heading shown when the annotation is selected. |
| **Text** | Longer body of text, shown as plain text in the viewer. |
| **Camera** | The [camera pose](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md) the viewer animates to when this annotation is selected. |
| **Extras** | Free-form metadata for custom integrations. Studio keeps it but has no control for editing it; set it in [imported settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md#saving-changes). |

## Adding an annotation

1. Frame the viewport the way you want a visitor to see this part of the scene.
2. Choose **Add annotation**: the button in the viewport toolbar, **Add** on the **Annotations** tab, or <kbd>C</kbd>.
3. Click the point on the splat you want to annotate. Studio places the hotspot there and stores the current view as the annotation's camera.
4. Type a title (**Untitled** until you do) and a description in the card that opens beside the hotspot, then click **OK**.

A scene can have up to 50 annotations, with titles of up to 60 characters and text of up to 280. These are the [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md#authoring-limits) authoring limits.

## Editing annotations

Select an annotation by clicking its hotspot or its row on the **Annotations** tab. Its card in the viewport has three buttons:

- **Edit annotation** (pencil) — change the title and description.
- **Set camera to current view** — store the current view as the annotation's camera.
- **Unselect annotation** — close the card.

While an annotation is selected, **Distance to camera** on the **Annotations** tab moves its hotspot along the view direction: <kbd>-</kbd> nudges it toward the camera and <kbd>+</kbd> away, and holding <kbd>Shift</kbd> makes finer steps. Use it to lift a hotspot off the surface or tuck it closer.

Each row on the **Annotations** tab also has **Go to annotation**, which moves the viewport to the annotation's camera, and **Delete annotation**. Drag rows to reorder them: the order controls how visitors step through the annotations, and the number each hotspot shows.

## How visitors use them

On the [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md), the viewer shows each annotation as a numbered hotspot. Selecting one eases the camera to the annotation's view and shows its title and text, and a navigator steps through the annotations in list order. [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#annotations) describes everything visitors can do with them.

[Video](https://developer.playcanvas.com/video/supersplat-annotations-visitor.mp4)

A visitor selects a hotspot, then steps through the annotations with the navigator. Honeybee by [danylyon](https://superspl.at/user/danylyon).

:::note

The settings format accepts `annotation` as a scene's start mode, but the viewer doesn't act on it: a scene always starts from its [starting camera](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md) or its camera animation.

:::

## See also

- [Cameras](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md) — the camera poses annotations reference
- [Camera animation (Timeline)](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md) — for cinematic flythroughs that don't need visitor interaction
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract that stores annotations

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Scene Page

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md

The **scene page** at `https://superspl.at/scene/<hash>` is the public face of a published splat. Whatever you authored in the [Editor](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor.md) and curated in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) shows up here for visitors. Owners see additional controls that open Studio or take them back to Manage.

Visitors can browse a scene page without a PlayCanvas account. An account is required to **like** the splat, **leave a comment** or **follow** its creator.

## What visitors see

The scene content is split between a central **embedded viewer** and a right-hand **sidebar** with metadata and actions.

[Image: The bumblebee splat's scene page — a central embedded viewer beside a sidebar of metadata and actions]

### The embedded viewer

The viewer is the open-source [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) rendered inside an iframe. The cameras, [camera animation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md), annotations, post effects, skybox, and collision you configured in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md), or published from the Editor, all apply here. Visitors can orbit, fly, and (if collision is set up) walk through the scene, step through annotations, play the camera animation, and enter VR or AR on devices that support it. The toolbar along the bottom of the viewer holds the camera modes and the viewer's settings, controls and info panels. See [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) and [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md).

### Sidebar metadata

| Field | What it shows |
|-------|---------------|
| **Title** | The headline you set in the [Edit Splat dialog](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md). |
| **Author** | A chip linking to the creator's [user profile](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/user-profile.md), with a **Follow** button so you can [follow them](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/user-profile.md#following). |
| **Views** | Total view count. |
| **Downloads** | Total download count. Only shown if the splat is downloadable. |
| **Visibility badge** | **Public** or **Unlisted**. |
| **Software used** | Chips for the tools you tagged in the Edit Splat dialog (capture / training tools). |
| **Description** | The longer description you set in the Edit Splat dialog (sanitized HTML). |
| **Format / size** | The published splat format and download size, with a tooltip. |
| **Splat count** | The number of Gaussians in the published splat. Its tooltip lists the levels of detail of a [streamed](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md) splat, and the spherical harmonic bands. |
| **Created** | Relative time the splat was published, with the exact date on hover. |

### Action buttons

| Button | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Like** (thumbs-up) | Shows the splat's like count and toggles your like. Highlighted if you've liked the splat. Requires login — anonymous visitors are prompted to sign in. |
| **Share** | Opens the [Share dialog](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md#share-dialog). |
| **Embed** | Opens the [Embed dialog](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md#embed-dialog). |
| **Download** | Opens the [Download dialog](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md#download-dialog). Only shown if the splat is downloadable. |

Owners also see an **Edit in Studio** entry point that opens [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) for this scene.

## Share dialog

The Share dialog gives one-click sharing to social platforms plus a copyable link.

| Action | Behavior |
|--------|----------|
| **Facebook / X / LinkedIn / Reddit** | Opens the platform's share intent prefilled with the scene's URL and title. |
| **Copy link** | Copies the scene URL to your clipboard with a brief **Copied!** confirmation. |

## Embed dialog

The Embed dialog gives you an `<iframe>` snippet to drop into your own webpage. The snippet points back at the scene's public URL so any future Studio updates show up automatically.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| **Iframe snippet** | A copy-to-clipboard `<iframe>` tag. |
| **Size presets** | Pick from a few common embed sizes or use a responsive layout. |

If you'd rather host your own copy of the viewer and bundle the splat into a self-contained file instead of pointing back at superspl.at, see [Self-Hosting the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md).

## Download dialog

The Download button is shown only when the owner has enabled **Downloadable** for the splat from the [Manage page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md). Click it to open the Download dialog, which offers:

| Section | Contents |
|---------|----------|
| **Targets** | A list of formats you can download — typically the original published format, a compressed PLY, a self-contained HTML viewer, and (if the scene has collision) a `voxel.zip`. Each entry shows its file size. |
| **License** | Expandable section with the Creative Commons license the owner picked. Shows the CC icons, a summary, an **Open License** link, and a **Copy Credit** button that produces ready-to-paste attribution text. |

:::note Preparation may take a moment

Some download targets are produced on demand — the dialog shows a **Preparing…** state while the file is built, then makes it available to download.

:::

## Comments

Below the viewer is the comments section. Anyone signed in can post a comment; the splat's owner can delete any comment.

- Each comment shows the commenter's avatar, username, timestamp, and sanitized HTML body.
- Comments can be liked individually (the per-comment thumbs-up icon).
- The comments list is paginated; up to **100 comments** are returned per page.
- Comments are sorted newest-first.

A PlayCanvas account is required to post — unauthenticated visitors see a prompt to sign in.

## Likes

The **Like** button (thumbs-up) in the action bar is a single-click toggle that also shows the like count. Counts update immediately. Like requires a PlayCanvas account; visitors without one are prompted to sign in.

## Suggested splats

A carousel near the bottom of the page recommends a handful of related splats. Click any card to navigate to its scene page.

## See also

- [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) — owners use Studio to change what visitors see here
- [Embedding the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md) — for full programmatic control of how the splat is displayed
- [Manage](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md) — edit metadata, change visibility, choose downloadable + license

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Viewer Controls

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md

The [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) is what visitors use on every [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md), in every embed of one, and in viewers [exported from the Editor](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md). This page describes its built-in interface. For headsets, and AR on phones, see [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md).

## Loading

While a scene loads, the viewer shows its poster image, if it has one, and a loading bar with a percentage. A [streamed scene](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md) appears as soon as it has enough detail to render and keeps refining as more streams in. [Collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md) data keeps loading in the background, and walk mode becomes available when it arrives.

The camera then starts moving. If the scene [plays its camera animation on open](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md#playing-on-open), that plays; otherwise the viewer plays a slow 20-second loop from the [starting camera](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md): an orbit around an object, or a gentle figure-eight inside a scene. Interacting with the scene stops it and hands the camera to the visitor.

## The toolbar

The toolbar runs along the bottom of the viewer. From left to right:

| Button | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| **Play** / **Pause** | Plays or pauses the camera animation. Shown only when the scene has one. While it plays, a timeline above the toolbar shows the playhead; drag it to scrub, which pauses playback. |
| **Orbit Camera** | Switches to [orbit mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#camera-modes). |
| **Fly Camera** | Switches to [fly mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#camera-modes). |
| **Walk Mode** | Switches to [walk mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#camera-modes), or back to the previous mode. Shown only on scenes that can be walked. |
| **Settings** | Opens the [settings panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#the-settings-panel). |
| **Controls** | Opens the [controls panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#the-controls-panel). |
| **Info** | Opens the [info panel](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#the-info-panel). |
| **Enter AR** / **Enter VR** | Starts an AR or VR session. Shown only where the device and browser support one. See [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md). |
| **Fullscreen** | Enters or leaves fullscreen. |

Three seconds after the last interaction the toolbar dims, then hides; the next interaction brings it back. It stays up while a panel is open or the pointer is over it. In a narrow viewer the buttons shrink so that all of them, **Fullscreen** included, stay in view. On a phone or tablet, turning the device to landscape requests fullscreen and turning it back to portrait leaves it.

## Camera modes

| Mode | Key | What it does |
|------|-----|--------------|
| **Orbit** | <kbd>1</kbd> | Circles the camera around a focus point. The starting mode for objects. |
| **Fly** | <kbd>2</kbd> | Moves the camera freely through the scene. |
| **Walk** | <kbd>3</kbd> | Walks on the scene's floor at eye height (1.5 m), with gravity and jumping. Needs [collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md) and a scene at least 5 m across. The starting mode for scenes that can be walked. |
| **Animation** | — | Plays the camera animation. **Play** selects it. |

The viewer treats a splat as an object when its starting camera is outside the splat's bounds, and as a scene when the camera starts inside. A scene that can't be walked starts in fly mode.

On a desktop, pressing <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>A</kbd>, <kbd>S</kbd> or <kbd>D</kbd> outside fly and walk mode switches to walk mode (fly mode where walking isn't available) and turns on **Gaming Controls**.

### Gaming Controls

Fly and walk mode have two control schemes. By default, you click or tap where you want to go and drag to look around. With **Gaming Controls** on:

- **On a desktop**, the viewer captures the mouse: moving it looks around, and <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> move. <kbd>Esc</kbd> releases the mouse and turns Gaming Controls off. <kbd>G</kbd> toggles them.
- **On a touch device**, a joystick appears for moving, and you drag to look around. Turn them on with the **Gaming Controls** switch in the settings panel.

## The controls panel

**Controls** opens a panel above the toolbar that lists the controls for the current camera mode, for whichever you last used: mouse and keyboard, or touch. It updates as you switch modes or turn Gaming Controls on and off. The panel is open for a first-time visitor, and the viewer remembers when it's closed. <kbd>H</kbd> toggles it.

[Image: The Controls panel open above the viewer toolbar during a camera animation]

The panel lists these controls. Touch has none for the camera animation: any touch takes over.

### Orbit mode

| Action | Mouse and keyboard | Touch |
|--------|--------------------|-------|
| **Orbit** | Left-drag | One finger drag |
| **Pan** | Right-drag | Two finger drag |
| **Zoom** | Mouse wheel | Pinch |
| **Set Focus** | Click | Tap |
| **Fly to Point** | Double-click | Double-tap |
| **Frame Scene** | <kbd>F</kbd> | — |
| **Reset Camera** | <kbd>R</kbd> | — |

### Fly mode

| Action | Mouse and keyboard | Touch |
|--------|--------------------|-------|
| **Fly To** | Click | Tap |
| **Look Around** | Left-drag | Touch + drag |
| **Pan** | Right-drag | — |
| **Focus Point** | Double-click | Double-tap |
| **Move** | <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> | Pinch / two finger drag |
| **Run / Slow** | <kbd>Shift</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> | — |
| **Reset Camera** | <kbd>R</kbd> | — |

With Gaming Controls on, **Look Around** is the captured mouse (or touch + drag), **Move** is <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> (or the joystick), **Vertical** is <kbd>Q</kbd> / <kbd>E</kbd>, and <kbd>Esc</kbd> is **Release Mouse**.

### Walk mode

| Action | Mouse and keyboard | Touch |
|--------|--------------------|-------|
| **Walk To** | Click | Tap |
| **Look Around** | Left-drag | Touch + drag |
| **Fly to Point** | Double-click | Double-tap |
| **Move** | <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> | — |
| **Run / Slow** | <kbd>Shift</kbd> / <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> | — |
| **Reset Camera** | <kbd>R</kbd> | — |
| **Exit Walk** | <kbd>Esc</kbd> | — |

With Gaming Controls on, **Look Around** is the captured mouse (or touch + drag), **Move** is <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> (or the joystick), **Jump** is <kbd>Space</kbd> (or a tap), and <kbd>Esc</kbd> is **Release Mouse**.

### Animation

| Action | Mouse and keyboard |
|--------|--------------------|
| **Play / Pause** | <kbd>Space</kbd> |
| **Exit / Cancel** | <kbd>Esc</kbd> |

## The settings panel

[Image: The Settings panel with the Quality slider and Performance Mode]

**Settings** opens a panel above the toolbar:

| Setting | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Show Annotations** | Shows or hides the [annotation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#annotations) hotspots and navigator. Shown only on scenes with annotations. |
| **Show Collision** | Draws the scene's collision geometry over the splat (<kbd>V</kbd>). Shown only when the scene's collision can be drawn: voxel collision needs WebGPU. |
| **Gaming Controls** | Turns on [Gaming Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#gaming-controls). Shown on touch devices; on a desktop, use <kbd>G</kbd>. |
| **Quality** | A slider with four positions, **Performance**, **Default**, **High** and **Max**, labeled with the Gaussian budget each gives, such as **Default · 4M**. See [Quality](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#quality). |
| **Performance Mode** | Switches to the viewer's alternative splat renderer. See [Performance Mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#performance-mode). |
| **Frame** | Frames the whole scene, in orbit mode. |
| **Reset** | Resets the camera: in orbit mode to the starting view, in fly and walk mode to where you entered that mode. |

The viewer saves **Show Annotations**, **Gaming Controls**, **Quality** and **Performance Mode** in the browser, so they carry over to every scene the visitor opens on the same site.

### Quality

The **Quality** slider sets the Gaussian budget, the most Gaussians the viewer draws at once in a streamed scene, from a ladder for the device: for example 2M, 4M, 8M and 16M on a desktop. At **Performance**, the viewer also renders at half resolution. [Streaming & Performance](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md#near-instant-loads-and-the-gaussian-budget) lists every device's ladder and starting position, and explains how the budget works.

### Performance Mode

**Performance Mode** draws the Gaussians with a different renderer that doesn't sort them. Its image refines over a few frames once the camera stops moving. It's off by default and offered only on WebGPU, and not in the Meta Quest or Pico browsers.

## The info panel

**Info** (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd>) shows the viewer's version, the renderer (**WebGPU** or **WebGL 2**) and GPU in use, and the PlayCanvas Engine version. On a desktop it also lists the global keyboard shortcuts.

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| <kbd>1</kbd> | Orbit mode |
| <kbd>2</kbd> | Fly mode |
| <kbd>3</kbd> | Walk mode, or back to the previous mode |
| <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> | Move; outside fly and walk mode, switches to walk (or fly) with Gaming Controls |
| <kbd>G</kbd> | Toggle Gaming Controls |
| <kbd>V</kbd> | Show Collision |
| <kbd>F</kbd> | Frame Scene (not in walk mode) |
| <kbd>R</kbd> | Reset Camera |
| <kbd>Space</kbd> | Play / Pause (Jump in walk mode) |
| <kbd>H</kbd> | Toggle the controls panel |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd> | Toggle the info panel |
| <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Release the mouse, leave walk mode, or close a panel |

Shortcuts follow the characters your keyboard layout types. On a layout that doesn't type Latin characters, such as Cyrillic or Greek, they fall back to the key positions of a US layout. <kbd>W</kbd> <kbd>A</kbd> <kbd>S</kbd> <kbd>D</kbd> always use the key positions.

## Annotations

Scenes with [annotations](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md) show a numbered hotspot for each one.

- **Click or tap a hotspot** to select it. The camera eases to the annotation's view, and its title and text appear in a panel beside the hotspot as the camera arrives. An annotation with neither title nor text shows no panel. Orbiting from there pivots near the annotated point, and the panel stays open.
- **Step through annotations** with the navigator's previous and next arrows, which show the annotation's number and title. The navigator appears when a scene has two or more annotations and wraps around at either end.
- **Click elsewhere in the viewer** to deselect. A drag doesn't count, so orbiting leaves the selection alone. The navigator keeps the last annotation, greyed out; click it to select it again.

Hotspots that part of the scene hides are faded, once the camera stops moving. **Show Annotations** in the settings panel hides the hotspots and the navigator.

## See also

- [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md) — headsets and AR on phones
- [Streaming & Performance](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md) — streamed scenes and the Gaussian budget
- [Scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) — where visitors meet the viewer on superspl.at
- [Viewer API](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md) — control the same features from your own code
