## Viewing in VR and AR

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md

The [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) supports WebXR. On a headset, or a phone whose browser supports AR, visitors can step into a splat in VR or place it in the room around them in AR. It works the same on [scene pages](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md), embeds, and [self-hosted](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md) viewers.

## Entering a session

**Enter AR** and **Enter VR** appear in the [toolbar](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#the-toolbar) when the browser supports them, and become available once the scene has loaded. To leave, choose **Exit VR** or **Exit AR** in the [menu](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#the-menu), or use the browser's own controls.

Some browsers can host a session with WebGL but not WebGPU. When the viewer is running on WebGPU in such a browser, the button opens a **WebGL Required** dialog instead; **OK** reloads the viewer with WebGL, adding `webgl` to the page URL.

On Apple Vision Pro, Safari can leave a VR request waiting. The viewer then shows **Nothing happening? Switch tabs and back.**

:::tip Start in VR

When you host the viewer yourself, the `vr` [URL parameter](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters) shows a **Tap to enter VR** prompt while the scene loads. Tapping it starts a VR session as soon as the scene is placed, and the rest of the scene streams in during the session. The camera animation starts paused.

:::

## What changes in a session

- The session starts where the viewer's camera is, facing the way it looks.
- [Post effects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects.md) aren't drawn. The scene's tone mapping still is.
- In AR, the [skybox](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md#skybox) and background are hidden, so the room shows through.
- A [streamed scene](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md) chooses its detail by distance alone, so turning your head doesn't stream new detail.
- On Meta Quest and Pico headsets, sessions render with fixed foveation, target 72 Hz where the headset supports it, and use a lower Gaussian budget (see [Streaming & Performance](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/streaming.md#near-instant-loads-and-the-gaussian-budget)). At the **Performance** quality position they also render at 0.8× resolution.
- The [collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md) overlay is turned off.

When the session ends, the splat goes back to its authored placement and the viewer's own settings return.

## Scenes and objects

The viewer treats a splat as an **object** when its [starting camera](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md) is outside the splat's bounds, such as a statue or a product scan, and as a **scene** when the camera starts inside it, such as a room or a landscape.

- **A scene in VR** surrounds you at real size. You move through it by [teleporting](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#moving-around-in-vr), and grabbing it moves and scales you, so you stay on its floor.
- **An object** is placed in front of you at about table height, up to 80 cm across and turned to show the side the starting camera showed. You handle it with [grabbing](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#grabbing-turning-and-scaling) rather than teleporting.
- **In AR**, every splat is handled as an object. A scene becomes a miniature diorama.

## Moving around in VR

To **teleport**, point a hand or controller at the floor, pinch or hold the trigger to show an arc, and let go to move to where it lands.

- **With collision**, walls and furniture stop the arc, a spot is a valid target only where you could stand, and a grid of the floor around the target shows where you'll land.
- **Without collision**, the arc lands on the floor visible in the splats, and a faint grid around your feet shows where that floor is.

With controllers, you can also move with the left thumbstick and turn with the right.

To **recenter**, hold the Meta button on a Quest or the Digital Crown on Apple Vision Pro. This returns you to where the session started, at real size.

## Grabbing, turning and scaling

Squeeze both grips, or make fists with both tracked hands, then move your hands together:

- **Move** your hands to drag.
- **Turn** your hands around each other to rotate.
- **Spread** them apart or bring them together to scale.

In a VR scene this moves and scales *you*: from a quarter to four times your real size, so you can shrink a whole environment into a model in front of you. An object, and any splat in AR, moves, turns and scales about its base, from a quarter to four times its placed size.

## Placing a splat in AR

When an AR session starts, the splat appears in front of you, drawn faintly, with a hint for your input:

| Input | Hint |
|-------|------|
| Tracked hands | **Pinch, point at a floor or table, then let go** |
| Controllers | **Hold the trigger, point at a floor or table, then let go** |
| A phone | **Touch a floor or table to place, two fingers to resize and turn** |

A ring shows where the splat will land. Only roughly level surfaces, such as a floor or a table top, take it. Once placed, the splat stands on a soft shadow; place it again the same way, or [grab it](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#grabbing-turning-and-scaling) to move, turn and scale it.

## Ice-cream mode

With tracked hands, hold your left fist upright, look at it and keep your right hand open. After two seconds, the splat sits on top of your fist like an ice cream: a scene in miniature, or an object about 15 cm across.

- Twist or tip your wrist to turn it.
- Close your right fist and move it to resize the splat, or swing it around your left fist to spin it.
- Open your left hand to put the splat back.

With controllers, squeeze the left grip while holding the controller upright: the splat stands on the controller's top face, and the right grip resizes and turns it.

Ice-cream mode is on by default. Turn it off with **Ice-cream mode** in the menu.

## The menu

The menu holds the viewer's settings during a session.

- **With tracked hands**, hold one palm open and facing you. The menu appears beside it; poke a row with the other hand's index fingertip.
- **With controllers**, press the X or A button to open or close the menu on that controller, then point at a row with the other controller and pull the trigger.
- **On Apple Vision Pro**, look at a row and pinch.

| Row | What it does |
|-----|--------------|
| **Reset Camera** | Returns you to where the session started, and puts a moved object back in front of you. |
| **Quality** | Steps through the [quality positions](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#quality) the session can hold: the left half of the row steps down, the right half up. |
| **Performance Mode** | Switches [Performance Mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#performance-mode). Shown where it's offered. |
| **Ice-cream mode** | Turns [ice-cream mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#ice-cream-mode) on or off. Shown with hands or controllers. |
| **Exit VR** / **Exit AR** | Ends the session. |

Controllers that also report a hand, such as Steam Frame's, work as controllers.

## See also

- [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) — the viewer's toolbar and panels outside a session
- [Collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md) — make a scene walkable, and teleportable in VR
- [Viewer API](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md#fullscreen-and-xr) — start and end sessions from your own code

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## SuperSplat Viewer

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md

The **SuperSplat Viewer** is the open-source web viewer that renders every [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) on superspl.at. It takes a splat plus a settings JSON document and turns them into an interactive 3D experience: orbit, fly and walk camera modes, annotations, camera animations, post effects, collision for walkable scenes, and VR and AR on devices that support WebXR.

The viewer is [open source on GitHub](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-viewer) under the MIT license and is distributed on npm as [`@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer).

[Image: A blog post with the SuperSplat Viewer embedded in it]

## Using the viewer

Visitors see the same viewer wherever it runs: on a scene page, in an embed, or in a viewer exported from the Editor.

- [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) — the toolbar, camera modes, the controls, settings and info panels, keyboard shortcuts and annotations
- [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md) — entering a session, teleporting, grabbing and scaling, placing a splat in AR, and the hand menu

## When to use the viewer directly

The published [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) on superspl.at is usually the easiest way to share a splat. Reach for the viewer directly when you want:

- **A page without superspl.at chrome.** Embed the viewer in your own website, app, or product with your own surrounding UI.
- **Full control over how the viewer is configured.** Override the settings, content, skybox, poster image or collision via URL parameters, your own `settings.json`, or code.
- **Control from your own code.** Create viewers inside your web app, drive playback, the camera, annotations, fullscreen and XR, or replace the built-in UI with your own.
- **A self-contained, offline-friendly bundle.** Use the [Editor's HTML export](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md) to ship a single-file viewer alongside the splat.
- **Independence from superspl.at.** Self-host the viewer on your own infrastructure — no requests back to PlayCanvas servers at runtime.

## Ways to use it

| Form | Use when |
|------|----------|
| **Embed from superspl.at** | The splat is published on superspl.at and an `<iframe>` is enough. Use the [Embed dialog](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md#embed-dialog) on its scene page. |
| **HTML export from the Editor** | You want a self-contained `.html` (or a `.zip` of the viewer plus the splat) that you can email, drop on a USB stick, or host on GitHub Pages. See [Self-Hosting the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md). |
| **The prebuilt viewer from npm** | You want to serve the viewer's files yourself and point each page at a splat and `settings.json` with URL parameters. See [Embedding the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#hosting-the-prebuilt-viewer). |
| **`renderViewerHtml`** | Your server or build generates the page around the viewer, with the asset URLs and settings filled in. See [Embedding the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#generating-a-page). |
| **`createViewer`** | Your web app owns the page and creates, controls and destroys viewers itself. See [Viewer API](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md). |

Every form reads the same [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) JSON, so anything you authored in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) carries through.

## See also

- [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) — how visitors navigate a scene
- [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md) — headsets and AR on phones
- [Embedding](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md) — npm package, URL parameters, generated pages, settings.json
- [Viewer API](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md) — `createViewer` and controlling a viewer from code
- [Self-Hosting](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md) — exporting a single-file HTML viewer from the Editor
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract that drives the viewer

## Embedding the Viewer

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md

The [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) is published on npm as [`@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer). You can host the prebuilt viewer and configure it with URL parameters, generate a page around it, or create viewers inside your own web app.

If your splat is already published on superspl.at, the simplest embed is an `<iframe>` from the [Embed dialog](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md#embed-dialog) on its scene page.

## Choosing an approach

| Approach | Use when |
|----------|----------|
| [Host the prebuilt viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#hosting-the-prebuilt-viewer) | You want to serve the viewer's static files and point them at a splat and `settings.json`, configuring each page with URL parameters. |
| [Generate a page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#generating-a-page) with `renderViewerHtml` | Your server or build writes the HTML page, with the asset URLs and settings filled in. |
| [Create a viewer in your page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#creating-a-viewer-in-your-own-page) with `createViewer` | Your web app owns the page, and creates, controls and destroys viewers itself. |

## Installing

```bash
npm install @playcanvas/supersplat-viewer
```

The package has these entry points:

| Import | Provides |
|--------|----------|
| `@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer` | `renderViewerHtml`, and the viewer's stylesheet and bundle as the strings `css` and `js` |
| `@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/viewer` | `createViewer`, with `playcanvas` (2.24.1 or later) as a peer dependency |
| `@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/viewer.css` | The stylesheet `createViewer` needs |
| `@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/settings` | Settings types, defaults, validation and migration. See [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md#generating-and-validating-settings). |

The main entry also exports the viewer's page as the string `html`, but it is deprecated: its formatting changes between releases, so use `renderViewerHtml` instead.

## Hosting the prebuilt viewer

The package's `public/` folder holds the standalone viewer: `index.html`, `index.js`, `index.css`, and the WebAssembly decoders (`.wasm` files) that some formats need. Copy the folder to your web server and open `index.html`. With no parameters, it loads `./settings.json` and `./scene.compressed.ply` from beside it.

The `.wasm` files are fetched only for content that needs them, such as version 4 `.spz` files. Serve them as `application/wasm`.

### URL parameters

Configure each page with query parameters, for example `index.html?content=./museum/lod-meta.json&settings=./museum/settings.json`. These parameters are subject to change as the viewer evolves; the [project README](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-viewer#readme) lists the current set, along with a few more for developers.

#### Content

| Parameter | Description | Default |
| --------- | ----------- | ------- |
| `settings` | URL of the [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) JSON file | `./settings.json` |
| `content` | URL of the splat. See [Supported content](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#supported-content). | `./scene.compressed.ply` |
| `skybox` | URL of an equirectangular skybox image | _(none)_ |
| `poster` | URL of an image shown, blurred, while the scene loads | _(none)_ |
| `collision` | URL of collision data for walk mode: a `.voxel.json` file (with its `.voxel.bin` beside it), or a `.glb` mesh. `voxel` is an alias. | _(none)_ |

#### UI

| Parameter | Description |
| --------- | ----------- |
| `noui` | Hide the viewer's built-in UI |
| `noanim` | Start with the camera animation paused |
| `reticle` | Show a center reticle in fly and walk mode while the mouse is captured |
| `ministats` | Show runtime CPU/GPU performance graphs |
| `lang` | The UI language: `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, `ja`, `ko`, `pt-BR`, `ru` or `zh-CN`. By default, the browser's language. |
| `vr` | Show a **Tap to enter VR** prompt while the scene loads, where VR is available. See [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#entering-a-session). |

#### Rendering

| Parameter | Description |
| --------- | ----------- |
| `webgl` | Use WebGL. By default the viewer uses WebGPU where it's available. |
| `aa` | Force the anti-aliasing compensation for splats trained with anti-aliasing: `aa`, `aa=1`, `aa=true` or `aa=enable` turn it on for every splat, any other value turns it off. Without it, each splat file's own training mode decides. |
| `hpr` | Override the settings' `highPrecisionRendering`: `hpr`, `hpr=1`, `hpr=true` or `hpr=enable` turn it on, any other value off. |
| `nofx` | Turn off post effects |
| `budget` | The Gaussian budget, in millions, overriding every [Quality](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#quality) position |
| `fullload` | Load all of a streamed scene's detail before the first frame |
| `stochastic` | Experimental. Force the stochastic splat renderer that [Performance Mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#performance-mode) uses: `stochastic` in its per-pixel mode, `stochastic=mobile` in its mode for phones and headsets, or `stochastic=off` to keep the standard renderer. Each hides the Performance Mode setting. WebGPU only. |
| `colorize` | Color the Gaussians by level of detail |
| `heatmap` | Draw the collision overlay as a heat map. Needs WebGPU and voxel collision; turn the overlay on with **Show Collision** or <kbd>V</kbd>. |
| `debug` | Open the developer debug panel on load (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>D</kbd> toggles it) |

### Supported content

The viewer picks the format from the content's file name:

| Format | File |
|--------|------|
| PLY | `.ply`, `.compressed.ply` |
| SOG | `.sog`, or the `meta.json` of an unbundled SOG |
| Streamed SOG | `lod-meta.json` |
| SPZ | `.spz` (versions 3 and 4) |
| XGRIDS LCC2 | `.lcc2`, streamed on demand like a Streamed SOG |

SOG v3 files written by splat-transform 3.11.0 or 3.11.1 use an earlier layout that the viewer no longer reads. Convert them again with a current [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md).

## Generating a page

If your server or build generates the page around the viewer, use `renderViewerHtml`. It returns a complete HTML document, with your asset URLs and settings supplied in a single JSON block:

```ts
import { renderViewerHtml } from '@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer';

const page = renderViewerHtml({
    bootstrap: {
        settings,                      // an object, or omit it and set settingsUrl
        contentUrl: 'scene.sog',
        posterUrl: 'poster.jpg'
    },
    baseHref: '/viewer/',              // serving from a sub-path
    backgroundColor: [0, 0, 0],        // components are 0..1, not 0..255
    headExtras: '<script src="analytics.js"></script>',
    inlineCss: true                    // no sibling index.css needed
});
```

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `bootstrap` | The page's assets and settings: `settings` or `settingsUrl`, `contentUrl`, `contentFilename`, `posterUrl`, `skyboxUrl`, `collisionUrl` and `zstdDecoderUrl` |
| `baseHref` | The page's base URL, for serving the viewer from a sub-path |
| `backgroundColor` | The page background before the first frame, as 0–1 RGB like the settings' `background.color` |
| `headExtras` / `bodyStartExtras` | Markup added to the `<head>`, or at the start of the `<body>` |
| `inlineCss` / `inlineJs` | Inline the stylesheet or the bundle instead of loading `index.css` and `index.js` from beside the page |

Called with no options, it returns the page the package ships, unchanged. URL parameters on the served page still override the bootstrap's asset URLs, so each instance stays configurable, except inline `settings`, which take precedence over `?settings=`.

For a single self-contained file, set both `inlineCss` and `inlineJs`, pass the settings inline, and pass the splat as a `data:` URI in `contentUrl`. A `data:` URI has no file name, so name the content with `contentFilename`, such as `scene.sog`:

```ts
const page = renderViewerHtml({
    bootstrap: {
        settings,
        contentUrl: sogDataUri,
        contentFilename: 'scene.sog'
    },
    inlineCss: true,
    inlineJs: true
});
```

A single-file page that loads a version 4 `.spz` file also needs the decoder inline: set `zstdDecoderUrl` to `zstd-decoder.wasm` as a `data:` URL. `zstdDecoderUrl` has no URL parameter, since a link could otherwise run any WebAssembly in your page's origin.

## Creating a viewer in your own page

If your web app owns the page, create the viewer inside one of its elements:

```ts
import { createViewer } from '@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/viewer';
import '@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/viewer.css';

const viewer = await createViewer({
    container: document.getElementById('viewer'),
    settings: './settings.json',
    contentUrl: './scene.sog'
});

// later
viewer.destroy();
```

The returned handle controls loading, playback, the camera, annotations, fullscreen and XR, and the built-in UI can be restyled or replaced. See [Viewer API](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md).

## Settings JSON

The `settings` parameter or option points at an [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) v2 document, the same JSON format [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) saves. This is the complete document that `defaultSettings()` from `@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/settings` generates:

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "tonemapping": "linear",
  "highPrecisionRendering": false,
  "background": {
    "color": [0, 0, 0]
  },
  "postEffectSettings": {
    "sharpness": { "enabled": false, "amount": 0 },
    "bloom":     { "enabled": false, "intensity": 0.1, "blurLevel": 2 },
    "grading":   { "enabled": false, "brightness": 1, "contrast": 1, "saturation": 1, "tint": [1, 1, 1] },
    "vignette":  { "enabled": false, "intensity": 0.5, "inner": 0.3, "outer": 0.75, "curvature": 1 },
    "fringing":  { "enabled": false, "intensity": 0.5 }
  },
  "animTracks": [],
  "cameras": [
    { "initial": { "position": [0, 2, 0], "target": [2, 2, 0], "fov": 85 } }
  ],
  "annotations": [],
  "startMode": "default"
}
```

That camera looks across a captured space from inside it; `defaultSettings('object')` frames a subject from outside instead. For every field, the authoring limits, and the helpers for generating, validating and migrating settings, see the [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) reference.

## Programmatic publishing

To publish splats to superspl.at from your own pipeline instead of the Editor, use the [SuperSplat API](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/api-integrations.md). A scene published this way starts with the default settings, and its viewing experience is curated in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md).

- [SuperSplat Viewer overview](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) — what the viewer is and when to reach for it

## Viewer API

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md

`createViewer` creates a [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) inside an element of your own page and returns a handle for controlling it. Use it when your web app owns the page: to mount and unmount viewers in a component, run several on one page, drive the viewer from your own controls, or replace its UI. For a page that only shows one splat, the [prebuilt viewer or `renderViewerHtml`](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md) is simpler.

The package's [API reference](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/blob/main/docs/api.md) has further detail.

## Creating a viewer

Install the package and the PlayCanvas Engine, which the `/viewer` entry uses as a peer dependency (version 2.24.1 or later), so your copy of the engine is the one it runs on:

```bash
npm install @playcanvas/supersplat-viewer playcanvas
```

```ts
import { createViewer } from '@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/viewer';
import '@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/viewer.css';

const viewer = await createViewer({
    container: document.getElementById('viewer'),   // you size it; the viewer fills it
    settings: './settings.json',                    // a URL, a settings object, or a promise of one
    contentUrl: './scene.sog',
    posterUrl: './poster.jpg'                       // optional
});
```

The viewer builds its own canvas, UI and icons inside the container, so **the container needs a size**: an element with no height renders nothing.

`createViewer` resolves once the graphics device exists and loading has started, not when the scene is visible. Wait for `loaded` before calling the camera, playback and annotation commands:

```ts
viewer.events.on('progress:changed', (progress) => console.log(`${progress}%`));
viewer.events.on('loaded:changed', () => console.log('first frame rendered'));
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `container` | The element the viewer builds itself in. Required. |
| `settings` | The [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md): a URL, an object in any supported version, or a promise of one. Required. |
| `contentUrl` | The splat to load. Required. Any [supported format](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#supported-content); a `data:` URI works too. |
| `contentFilename` | A name for the content, such as `scene.sog`. The format is chosen from the name's extension, so set this when `contentUrl` has no usable name, such as a `data:` URI. |
| `posterUrl` / `poster` | An image shown, blurred, while the splat loads, as a URL or an already-created `HTMLImageElement`. |
| `skyboxUrl` | An equirectangular skybox image. |
| `collisionUrl` | Collision data for walk mode: a `.glb` mesh, or voxel data. |
| `contents` | A `fetch` of `contentUrl` already in flight, so the download can start before the viewer's code arrives. |
| `zstdDecoderUrl` | Where to load the version 4 `.spz` decoder from. See [Decoder files](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md#decoder-files). |

The remaining options are the programmatic form of the [URL parameters](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters), with the same names, except:

- `renderer: 'webgl'` forces WebGL, like `webgl`. The default is `'webgpu'`, which falls back to WebGL where WebGPU isn't available.
- `ui: false` leaves out the built-in UI, like `noui`. See [Replacing the UI](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md#replacing-the-ui).
- `exposeGlobals: true` publishes the viewer's `window.app`, `window.captureFrame` and similar hooks. Leave it off when a page has more than one viewer.

`createViewer` doesn't read the page's URL: pass every option yourself.

## The viewer handle

| Member | Purpose |
|--------|---------|
| `state` | The viewer's [observable state](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md#state). |
| `events` | Fires `<key>:changed` with `(value, previous)` for every key of `state`. |
| `annotations` | The scene's annotations in settings order, read-only. |
| `captureFrame(options?)` | Renders a still offscreen, supersampled, and resolves to `{ width, height, data }` with `data` in base64. Options: `time`, `width` (default 480), `height`, `supersample` (default 2). |
| `seek(time)` | Seeks the animation, in seconds, keeping its pause state. |
| `frameScene()` | Frames the whole scene in orbit mode. |
| `resetCamera()` | In fly or walk mode, returns to where that mode was entered; otherwise restores the starting view in orbit mode. |
| `toggleWalk()` | Enters walk mode, or returns to the previous mode. Does nothing unless `state.walkAllowed`. |
| `selectAnnotation(index)` | Selects an annotation by zero-based index and moves the camera to it; `null` clears the selection without moving the camera. |
| `setMoveInput(x, z)` | Holds camera-relative movement in fly or walk mode, for a custom joystick: positive `x` is right, positive `z` forward, each from -1 to 1. Send `(0, 0)` to stop. |
| `requestFullscreen()` / `exitFullscreen()` | Enters or leaves fullscreen for this viewer. |
| `startXR(mode)` / `endXR()` | Starts an immersive session, with `mode` `'ar'` or `'vr'`, or ends it. |
| `destroy()` | Releases the engine application, the graphics context, every listener and the viewer's elements. Safe to call more than once, and before loading finishes. |
| `app` | The underlying PlayCanvas application, for anything this API doesn't cover. |

The camera, playback, annotation and movement commands throw before `state.loaded` and after `destroy()`. The fullscreen and XR commands return promises; call the ones that enter fullscreen or a session from a user gesture, such as a click, and handle their rejections.

## State

Write a writable key and the change takes effect at once; the built-in UI follows it. The read-only keys report what the viewer found or is doing.

| Key | Writable | Description |
|-----|----------|-------------|
| `loaded` | | True once the first complete frame has rendered. |
| `progress` | | Loading progress, 0 to 100. |
| `cameraMode` | ✓ | `'orbit'`, `'fly'`, `'walk'` or `'anim'` (the camera animation). |
| `walkAllowed` | | Whether walk mode is available: collision data and a scene at least 5 m across. |
| `hasCollision` | | Whether collision data has loaded. |
| `hasCollisionOverlay` | | Whether the collision can be drawn as an overlay. |
| `collisionOverlayEnabled` | ✓ | Draws the collision overlay. |
| `hasAnimation` | | Whether there's a camera animation to play. |
| `animationPaused` | ✓ | Whether playback is paused. |
| `animationTime` / `animationDuration` | | The playhead and length, in seconds. |
| `selectedAnnotation` | | The selected annotation's index, or `null`. Use `selectAnnotation()` to change it. |
| `showAnnotations` | ✓ | Shows the built-in hotspots. Saved. |
| `quality` | ✓ | The [Quality](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#quality) position: `'performance'`, `'default'`, `'high'` or `'max'`. Saved. |
| `qualityAvailable` | | The positions this device can hold. |
| `performanceMode` | ✓ | [Performance Mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#performance-mode). Saved. |
| `gamingControls` | ✓ | [Gaming Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md#gaming-controls). Saved. |
| `iceCream` | ✓ | [Ice-cream mode](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md#ice-cream-mode) in XR. Saved. |
| `inputMode` | | `'desktop'` or `'touch'`: what the visitor last used. |
| `controlsHidden` | ✓ | Hides the built-in controls. The viewer also sets it when idle. |
| `inputEnabled` | ✓ | Whether this viewer takes keyboard and gamepad input. |
| `isFullscreen` | | Whether this viewer is fullscreen. |
| `hasAR` / `hasVR` | | Whether an AR or VR session can start, now or after reloading with WebGL. |
| `canStartAR` / `canStartVR` | | Whether one can start on the current renderer. |
| `xrMode` | | `'ar'`, `'vr'` or `null`. |

Collision data arrives after the scene appears, so `walkAllowed` and `hasCollision` can change after `loaded`: watch their change events rather than reading them once.

### Saved preferences

`quality`, `performanceMode`, `gamingControls`, `showAnnotations` and `iceCream` are read from and saved to the browser's local storage, under keys shared by every viewer on your site's origin. A new viewer reads the saved values; viewers already on the page keep their own. The built-in UI also remembers whether its controls panel is open. If storage is blocked, the viewer works with defaults.

## Controlling the viewer

The built-in controls use the same commands as your code, so the two stay in step. Wait for `loaded` first:

```ts
const whenLoaded = (callback: () => void) => {
    if (viewer.state.loaded) callback();
    else viewer.events.once('loaded:changed', callback);
};
```

### Playback

```ts
// stop at three seconds
whenLoaded(() => {
    viewer.state.animationPaused = true;
    viewer.seek(3);
});

// resume, from any camera mode
viewer.state.cameraMode = 'anim';
viewer.state.animationPaused = false;
```

`seek()` wraps repeating tracks and clamps the others to their duration.

### The camera

Set `state.cameraMode` to switch between orbit, fly and animation. Check `state.walkAllowed` before walk mode, or call `toggleWalk()`, which also returns to the previous mode. `frameScene()` and `resetCamera()` start a camera move and return at once.

For custom directional controls, select fly or walk mode, then hold movement with `setMoveInput()` until the control is released:

```ts
viewer.state.cameraMode = 'fly';
viewer.setMoveInput(0, 1);    // forward

// on release, pointercancel or unmount:
viewer.setMoveInput(0, 0);
```

### Annotations

```ts
viewer.events.on('selectedAnnotation:changed', (index) => {
    const annotation = index === null ? null : viewer.annotations[index];
    console.log(annotation?.title);
});

whenLoaded(() => {
    if (viewer.annotations.length) viewer.selectAnnotation(0);
});
```

Selecting an annotation switches to orbit mode and moves the camera to the annotation's view without changing the animation's pause state. `state.showAnnotations` hides the built-in hotspots without clearing the selection.

### Fullscreen and XR

```ts
fullscreenButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
    viewer.requestFullscreen().catch(showError);
});
vrButton.addEventListener('click', () => {
    viewer.startXR('vr').catch(showError);
});
viewer.events.on('xrMode:changed', updateControls);
```

Check `state.canStartAR` and `state.canStartVR`, and subscribe to their change events, since the capability checks can finish after creation. `startXR()` rejects when the current renderer can't host the session; it never reloads the page.

The built-in **WebGL Required** dialog reloads the page with `?webgl` added. If your page creates the viewer and keeps the built-in UI, read that parameter and pass `renderer: 'webgl'`. See [Viewing in VR and AR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md) for what visitors can do in a session.

## Restyling

The colors the built-in UI uses are CSS custom properties on the viewer's root element, so you can retheme it without replacing anything:

```css
#viewer .sse-viewer {
    --sse-accent: #09f;     /* highlights, active toggles, the timeline */
    --sse-bkg: #204;        /* panels; translucent surfaces derive from it */
    --sse-text-light: #fff;
}
```

The full set is `--sse-text`, `--sse-text-light`, `--sse-text-dark`, `--sse-text-darkest`, `--sse-accent`, `--sse-grip`, `--sse-bkg`, `--sse-bkg-dark`, `--sse-bkg-darkest` and `--sse-bkg-light`. The viewer's other class names aren't part of the API and change between releases.

## Replacing the UI

Pass `ui: false` to create only the canvas. Camera input on the canvas, keyboard and gamepad input, and saved preferences keep working; the toolbar, panels, poster, loading bar, annotation hotspots and navigator are left out. Build your own controls on the handle and its state. The touch joystick, the fullscreen button and the WebGL Required dialog are part of the UI you're replacing, so those become yours too: `setMoveInput()` supports a replacement joystick. Replacing only part of the built-in UI isn't supported.

The [custom UI example](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/blob/main/src/dev/custom-ui.html) in the viewer's repository drives loading, playback, camera modes, movement, annotations, preferences, fullscreen and XR through the handle alone.

## Several viewers on a page

Each viewer owns its own elements and its own engine application, and nothing is published to `window` unless you set `exposeGlobals`. Keyboard and gamepad input can't be routed by where the pointer is, so clear `state.inputEnabled` on the viewers that should ignore it, and while your own form fields have focus.

Always call `destroy()` on a viewer you no longer need. Browsers cap live WebGL contexts at around 16, so a component that mounts and unmounts viewers without destroying them stops rendering.

## Decoder files

Version 4 `.spz` files, on their own or as chunks of an `.lcc2` scene, need a WebAssembly decoder, `zstd-decoder.wasm`, which ships beside the viewer's bundle and is fetched only when such content loads. A bundler that handles `new URL(…, import.meta.url)` emits it with your bundle; otherwise serve it beside the bundle as `application/wasm`, or point `zstdDecoderUrl` at it. The decoder is loaded from a `blob:` URL, so a Content-Security-Policy must allow `blob:` scripts.

## See also

- [Embedding the Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md) — the npm package, URL parameters and `renderViewerHtml`
- [Viewer Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) — the built-in UI the handle drives
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the settings JSON and the helpers for generating it

## Self-Hosting the Viewer

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md

The [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) is [open source](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-viewer) and can be directly exported by the [SuperSplat Editor](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor.md) should you wish to self-host your splat content instead of (or in addition to) publishing to [superspl.at](https://superspl.at). The exported viewer runs in any modern web browser with the viewer's usual [controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/controls.md) and supports [AR and VR](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/xr.md) on devices that support WebXR.

## Exporting the HTML Viewer

To export your splat as an HTML viewer:

1. Open the `File` > `Export` submenu in the SuperSplat Editor.
2. Select `Viewer App…`.
3. Choose the output folder under **Location** and enter a **Filename**, set the options below, and click **Export**. The Editor remembers the folder for next time; in browsers without the File System Access API the file is delivered as a download instead.

The splat data is compressed to SOG on the GPU as part of the export, so large scenes take a moment.

## Export Options

The viewer export can be configured via several options:

[Image: Viewer Export]

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| **Export Type** | Controls the format of the exported viewer:<br/>• **HTML**: A single-page `.html` file where the splat is compressed to SOG, Base64 encoded and embedded directly into the file. Very convenient since everything is packed into a single file that can be double-clicked to run in your browser using the `file://` protocol. However, the base64 encoding means it will be roughly 30% larger than the ZIP Package format, and browsers impose different limits on the maximum size (below 32MB should load everywhere, but above this you could encounter problems)<br/>• **ZIP Package**: A zip file containing the viewer app (`index.html`, `index.js`, `index.css` and `settings.json`) plus the splat data as a bundled SOG file (`index.sog`). Smaller, loads faster and guaranteed to load everywhere. However, it will only load over `http://`, so you will need to run a local web server (e.g. Node's [`serve`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/serve) or Python's [`http.server`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.server.html) (`python -m http.server`)) |
| **Animation** | If enabled, the camera animation authored on the [Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md) is included and plays when the viewer loads. Only available when the Timeline has keyframes (and enabled by default in that case) |
| **Loop Mode** | How an included camera animation plays back:<br/>• **None**: Play once and stop<br/>• **Repeat**: Loop continuously<br/>• **Ping Pong**: Play forwards, then backwards, repeatedly<br/>Initialized from the Timeline's Loop toggle - **Repeat** if looping is enabled, **None** otherwise |
| **Background** | The background color of the viewer. Defaults to the Editor's **Background Color**, set in the **Colors** section of the [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences) popup |
| **Field of View** | The field of view of the viewer's camera in degrees, measured across the longer side of the screen. Defaults to the Editor camera's current setting |
| **SH Bands** | The exact number of spherical harmonics bands written to the exported splat data (0–3). Defaults to the highest band count in the scene, capped by the **SH Bands** setting in [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences). Choosing more bands than a splat contains fills the missing ones with zeros |

The exported viewer's camera starts at the pose your viewport camera has at the moment you export, so frame your favorite view before exporting.

Like the Editor's other exports, the exported splat is tagged with the anti-aliasing mode the viewport draws it with (see **Anti-Aliasing** in [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences)), and the viewer follows that tag.

## Web Hosting for the HTML Viewer

Once exported, you can host the HTML Viewer file somewhere to make it accessible. One easy option is to use GitHub Pages:

1. Create a new repository on [GitHub](https://github.com).
2. Add the exported HTML file (or, for a ZIP package, the extracted contents of the zip: `index.html`, `index.sog`, `index.js`, `index.css` and `settings.json`).
3. Visit your repository's `Settings` page. Select `Pages` on the left. Ensure `Source` is set to `Deploy from a branch` and set `Branch` to `main` and hit `Save`.
4. It will take a few moments for your viewer to be published. The URL will be in the form:

   `https://<github-username>.github.io/<repository-name>/<html-filename>`

## Other ways to self-host

The exported viewer is a copy of the viewer at the version the Editor includes, and doesn't update itself. To serve the latest viewer, or to point one copy at many splats, [host the prebuilt viewer from npm](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#hosting-the-prebuilt-viewer) and configure it with URL parameters. To produce the same HTML viewer from a script, use [splat-transform](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/splat-transform.md) with an `.html` output file.

## See also

- [SuperSplat Viewer overview](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) — what the open-source viewer is and when to use it
- [Embedding](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md) — using the `@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer` npm package in your own web app
- [Experience Settings](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md) — the JSON contract Studio writes and the Viewer reads

## Experience Settings

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/experience-settings.md

**Experience Settings** is the JSON document that defines a published splat's viewing experience — tonemapping, post effects, background, cameras, animations, annotations, and the scene's start mode. It's the single contract between two products:

- **Writer** — [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) saves it whenever you hit Save.
- **Reader** — the [SuperSplat Viewer](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer.md) loads it at runtime, both on the [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) and when [embedded](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md) or [self-hosted](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md).

You don't normally edit this JSON by hand — Studio is the supported authoring surface. But if you're embedding the Viewer in your own application, generating settings from a build pipeline, or consuming the published settings directly, the schema below is what to write against.

## Current schema (v2)

```typescript
type ExperienceSettings = {
    version: 2;

    tonemapping: 'none' | 'linear' | 'filmic' | 'hejl' | 'aces' | 'aces2' | 'neutral';
    highPrecisionRendering: boolean;
    soundUrl?: string;

    background: {
        color: [number, number, number]; // RGB, 0-1
        skyboxUrl?: string;              // optional .webp/.jpg/.png URL (see below)
    };

    postEffectSettings: {
        sharpness:  { enabled: boolean; amount: number };
        bloom:      { enabled: boolean; intensity: number; blurLevel: number };
        grading:    { enabled: boolean; brightness: number; contrast: number; saturation: number; tint: [number, number, number] };
        vignette:   { enabled: boolean; intensity: number; inner: number; outer: number; curvature: number };
        fringing:   { enabled: boolean; intensity: number };
    };

    cameras: Array<{                    // the viewer uses the first camera
        initial: {
            position: [number, number, number];
            target:   [number, number, number];
            fov:      number; // degrees
        };
    }>;

    animTracks: Array<{                 // the viewer plays the first track
        name: string;
        duration: number;       // seconds
        frameRate: number;
        loopMode: 'none' | 'repeat' | 'pingpong';
        interpolation: 'step' | 'spline';
        smoothness: number;     // 0-1
        keyframes: {
            times: number[];    // in frames, ascending
            values: {
                position: number[]; // flat array of [x, y, z] per keyframe
                target:   number[]; // flat array of [x, y, z] per keyframe
                fov:      number[]; // one FOV per keyframe
            };
        };
    }>;

    annotations: Array<{
        position: [number, number, number];
        title: string;
        text: string;                          // shown as plain text
        camera: { initial: { position: [number, number, number]; target: [number, number, number]; fov: number } };
        extras?: Record<string, unknown>;
    }>;

    // 'default'    — start at the first camera in `cameras`
    // 'animTrack'  — start by playing the first track in `animTracks`
    // 'annotation' — accepted, but the viewer currently starts as for 'default'
    startMode: 'default' | 'animTrack' | 'annotation';

    hasStartPose?: boolean;
};
```

Most fields are authored in a Studio control. The camera animation can also come from the SuperSplat Editor's Timeline, baked in at publish time. Follow the cross-references for details.

| Field | Authored in |
|-------|-------------|
| `tonemapping`, `highPrecisionRendering` | [Look & Tone](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md) |
| `background.color`, `background.skyboxUrl` | [Look & Tone](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md) |
| `postEffectSettings` | [Post Effects](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/post-effects.md) |
| `cameras` | [Cameras](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/cameras.md) |
| `animTracks` | [Camera Animation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md), or the [Editor Timeline](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/timeline.md) (baked in when publishing). Studio saves only a track that has keyframes. |
| `annotations` | [Annotations](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/annotations.md) |
| `startMode` | **Play animation on open** in the [Animation](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/animation.md#playing-on-open) section: `animTrack` when it is on, `default` when it is off. The initial value is set when publishing from the Editor. |
| `hasStartPose` | Set when publishing from the Editor |
| Collision voxel data | Stored separately as a [Scene Asset](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md), not in this JSON |

## How the viewer reads it

A few fields behave in ways the schema alone doesn't show:

- **`background.skyboxUrl`** — the viewer doesn't load the skybox from the settings. When you host the viewer yourself, pass the image with the `skybox` [URL parameter](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters) or the `skyboxUrl` option.
- **`soundUrl`** — the sound starts on the visitor's first click in the viewer, since browsers block audio that plays on its own.
- **`cameras` and `animTracks`** — the format allows several, but the viewer uses only the first camera and plays only the first track.
- **`annotations[].text`** — shown as plain text, so HTML markup isn't rendered.
- **`startMode: 'annotation'`** — accepted, but the viewer starts as it does for `default`.
- **`antiAlias`** — not part of the schema above, but Studio adds it: its [Anti-aliasing](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/look-and-tone.md#anti-aliasing) switch stores `antiAlias: false` when turned off. Scene pages and embeds on superspl.at apply it, with compensation on unless it's `false`. The open-source viewer doesn't read it from the settings file: there, the `aa` [URL parameter](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md#url-parameters) sets it, and without that each splat file's own anti-aliasing tag decides.

## Authoring limits

The viewer renders whatever the schema allows, but tools that write settings should keep to these bounds, which `validateSettings(settings, { limits: true })` checks:

| Field | Limit |
|-------|-------|
| Camera and annotation `fov` | 10 to 120 degrees |
| `annotations` | At most 50, each with a `title` of up to 60 characters and `text` of up to 280 |
| `animTracks` | At most 10, each with a `name` of up to 120 characters, a `duration` of 0.1 to 600 seconds, a whole `frameRate` of 1 to 120, a `smoothness` of 0 to 1, and 1 to 1,000 keyframes at whole, ascending frame numbers |
| `sharpness.amount` | 0 to 1 |
| `bloom.intensity` / `bloom.blurLevel` | 0 to 0.1 / 1 to 16 |
| `grading.brightness` / `contrast` / `saturation` | 0 to 3 / 0.5 to 1.5 / 0 to 2 |
| `vignette.intensity` / `inner` / `outer` / `curvature` | 0 to 1 / 0 to 3 / 0 to 3 / 0.01 to 10 |
| `fringing.intensity` | 0 to 100 |

Some settings already published fall outside these bounds, such as a `bloom.intensity` of `1` from older defaults, so the viewer doesn't enforce these limits when it loads a file.

## Generating and validating settings

The viewer's npm package exports the schema types and helpers from its `/settings` entry, so a pipeline can write settings the viewer accepts:

```ts
import {
    defaultSettings,
    importSettings,
    validateSettings,
    POST_EFFECT_RANGES,
    type ExperienceSettings
} from '@playcanvas/supersplat-viewer/settings';

// a complete settings object; pass 'object' to frame a subject from outside
const settings: ExperienceSettings = defaultSettings();

// throws on invalid input, naming the offending field
validateSettings(json);

// also check the authoring limits
validateSettings(json, { limits: true });

// migrates v1 settings to v2, without changing its argument
const migrated = importSettings(json);

// the bounds are data, so an editor UI can drive its sliders from them
const { min, max, step } = POST_EFFECT_RANGES.bloom.intensity;
```

`CAMERA_FOV_RANGE`, `POST_EFFECT_RANGES`, `ANIM_TRACK_LIMITS` and `ANNOTATION_LIMITS` export the limits above as data. `defaultSettings()` gives the camera an `85` degree field of view, at position `[0, 2, 0]` looking at `[2, 2, 0]`, or with `'object'`, at `[2, 2, -2]` looking at `[0, 0, 0]`.

## Defaults

A freshly-published splat is given a sensible default JSON:

- **Tonemapping** `linear`, **high precision** off
- **Background** `[0, 0, 0]` (black), no skybox
- **Post effects** all disabled
- **One camera** with FOV `75` — for environment-style scenes the default pose is position `[0, 2, 0]`, target `[2, 2, 0]`; for object-style scenes it's position `[2, 2, -2]`, target `[0, 0, 0]`
- **No animation tracks** and **no annotations**
- **Start mode** `default`

Studio surfaces these defaults the first time you open a scene; tweak as needed.

## Schema versioning

Older `v1` settings are migrated to `v2` automatically when loaded by Studio or the Viewer — you don't need to do anything special. If you're generating settings yourself, write `v2` and you're current.

## See also

- [Viewer / embedding](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/embedding.md) — how to point a Viewer at a `settings.json` URL
- [Viewer API](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/viewer-api.md) — pass settings to a viewer you create in your own page
- [Viewer / self-hosting](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/self-hosting.md) — exporting a self-contained Viewer that bundles a copy of these settings

## API & Integrations

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/api-integrations/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/developers/api-integrations.md

The SuperSplat API lets applications publish Gaussian splats to superspl.at, list the scenes owned by the authenticated user, look up any scene by id, and download scenes whose owners allow it. Use it to connect a capture application, training pipeline, conversion tool, or internal content workflow directly to SuperSplat.

Uploaded scenes appear on the user's [Manage page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md), where they can be edited, opened in [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md), or shared through their public [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md).

:::info Complete API reference

For endpoint definitions, request schemas, and response examples, see the [SuperSplat API reference](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/api/supersplat/).

:::

## When to use the API

The API is useful when you want to:

- Publish splats without opening the SuperSplat Editor.
- Add SuperSplat publishing to a capture or reconstruction application.
- Batch-upload output from a training or conversion pipeline.
- List the scenes owned by a user.
- Look up any scene by id, and import downloadable scenes into your own tools.
- Resume a large upload after an interrupted connection.

## Authentication

All API operations require a PlayCanvas access token. See [REST API authorization](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/api.md#authorization) to create a token, then send it in the `Authorization` header:

```http
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
```

Treat access tokens as secrets. Do not embed them in public client-side code or share them with another user.

## Resumable upload flow

SuperSplat uses multipart uploads so clients can reliably transfer large scene files:

1. Create an upload session with the source format and optional scene metadata.
2. Request signed upload URLs for one or more file parts.
3. Upload those parts directly to storage.
4. Complete the upload using the returned part ETags.

SuperSplat creates the scene after the upload is completed. The scene may remain in `processing` while conversion and optimization finish. New scenes are unlisted by default.

## Downloading scenes

`GET /v1/splats/{splatId}` returns any scene by id, whoever owns it, listed or unlisted. When its `downloadable` field is `true`, its owner allows downloads under a Creative Commons license (given in `license`), and `content` describes its published files. A download is the only way the API gives you a scene's files:

1. Request a download with `POST /v1/splats/{splatId}/downloads`, giving a `target` format the scene offers.
2. Poll `GET /v1/splats/{splatId}/downloads/{target}` until its `status` is `ready`. If it is `failed`, request the download again.
3. Get a short-lived URL with `POST /v1/splats/{splatId}/downloads/{target}/file`, and start fetching it before `urlExpiresAt`.

| `target` | Offered for | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ply` | Every downloadable scene | A conversion to a standard PLY |
| `sog` | Scenes published as SOG | The published SOG files, unchanged |
| `ssog` | Scenes published as Streamed SOG | The published Streamed SOG files with their levels of detail, unchanged |

Each download is a ZIP archive with the files at its root and a `license.txt` giving the scene's title, author, source and license. Downloads are shared and cached, so a scene someone downloaded recently is often `ready` straight away. A download lasts while the scene stays the same. Once the scene is republished, renamed or relicensed, the download returns `404` and you request it again.

Requesting and polling a download are free. Getting the file counts towards the account's daily download allowance, once per scene per UTC day.

## Limits

When a request goes over a limit, the API answers `429` with a `code` that says which. A `429` without a `code` means the client is sending requests too quickly.

| `code` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `daily_publish_limit_reached` | The account has used today's publishing allowance, measured in bytes of compressed output. It resets at 00:00 UTC. |
| `too_many_processing` | The account already has as many scenes uploading or processing as it may at once. |
| `publish_in_progress` | Another publish for the account is starting. |
| `daily_download_limit_reached` | The account has downloaded as many scenes as it may today (UTC). |

An upload larger than its source format allows is rejected with the largest size allowed. The [API reference](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/api/supersplat/) gives the fields of each error.

## Client integrations

The same API supports both end-user integrations and custom automation:

- The [**SuperSplat plugin for LichtFeld Studio**](https://github.com/playcanvas/supersplat-lichtfeld-plugin) exports PLY or SOG scenes and publishes them to SuperSplat with progress reporting and resumable uploads.

Clients can identify themselves through the optional `uploadClient` field:

```json
{
  "uploadClient": {
    "id": "example-client",
    "version": "1.0.0"
  }
}
```

Use `uploadClient` for the application performing the upload. Use `softwareTools` separately to record the tools used to create the scene.

## See also

- [SuperSplat API reference](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/api/supersplat/) — complete endpoint and schema documentation
- [Scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) — download a scene from its page on superspl.at
- [Direct Upload](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md) — publish a file through the superspl.at interface
- [Manage](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md) — work with uploaded scenes
- [Studio](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio.md) — curate the published viewing experience

## Camera Controls

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md

You navigate the Editor's 3D view with a mouse, touch, or the keyboard. There are two control modes: **Orbit** (default) and **Fly**.

- **Orbit mode** - Camera rotates around a focal point. Best for inspecting objects from all angles.
- **Fly mode** - Camera moves freely through the scene. Best for navigating large environments.

Press <kbd>V</kbd> to toggle between modes, or press <kbd>W</kbd>, <kbd>A</kbd>, <kbd>S</kbd> or <kbd>D</kbd> to switch to fly mode automatically.

## Mouse Controls

| Action | Orbit Mode | Fly Mode |
|--------|------------|----------|
| Left drag | Orbit around focal point | Look around |
| Middle click | Set focal point | — |
| Middle drag | Orbit around focal point | Look around |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> + middle drag | Pan | Pan |
| <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + middle drag | Zoom | Zoom |
| Right drag | Pan | Pan |
| Right + <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>/<kbd>Shift</kbd> drag | Orbit | Look around |
| Right + <kbd>Alt</kbd>/<kbd>Cmd</kbd> drag | Zoom | Zoom |
| Mouse wheel | Zoom | Move forward/backward |
| Mouse wheel + <kbd>Shift</kbd> | Pan | Pan |
| Mouse wheel + <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> | Orbit | Look around |
| Double-click | Set focal point | Set focal point (switches to orbit) |

## Touch Controls

| Action | Orbit Mode | Fly Mode |
|--------|------------|----------|
| Single finger drag | Orbit | Look around |
| Two-finger drag | Pan | — |
| Two-finger pinch/spread | Zoom | Move forward/backward |

## Keyboard Controls

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| <kbd>W</kbd> / <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>S</kbd> / <kbd>D</kbd> | Fly forward/left/backward/right |
| <kbd>Q</kbd> / <kbd>E</kbd> | Fly down/up |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd> | 10× faster fly speed |
| <kbd>Alt</kbd> | 0.1× slower fly speed |
| <kbd>V</kbd> | Toggle between orbit and fly modes |
| <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd> | Reset camera to default position |
| <kbd>F</kbd> | Focus camera on the selection (or on the active Box, Sphere, Measure, or Orient tool) |
| <kbd>I</kbd> | Toggle the [camera info overlay](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md#camera-info-overlay) |

## Camera Settings

Three settings in the [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences) popup (the gear icon in the right toolbar) affect the camera: **Field of View**, **FOV Auto Dolly**, and **Fly Speed**. Their ranges and defaults are listed under [Preferences](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/interface.md#preferences).

The field of view spans the longer side of the viewport: horizontally when the viewport is wider than it is tall, and vertically when it is taller than it is wide. Published scenes and exported viewers apply it the same way.

By default, changing the Field of View behaves like a lens zoom: the camera stays where it is and the scene appears magnified or shrunk. Enable **FOV Auto Dolly** to have the camera dolly (move) as the FOV changes instead, preserving the subject's framing.

## Camera Info Overlay

Press <kbd>I</kbd> (or enable **Camera Info** in the **Overlays** popup) to toggle an information overlay in the bottom-left corner of the viewport:

[Image: Camera Info Overlay]

The overlay shows the camera's live pose as `x, y, z` coordinates in scene units, updating in real time as you navigate:

- **P** - The camera's position
- **T** - The camera's target (the focal point it orbits around)

### Setting the Camera Pose Numerically

Both values are editable, so you can place the camera precisely:

1. Click a value - the text is selected, ready to overwrite
2. Type three numbers separated by commas or spaces (for example, `-0.55, 0.8, 1.1`)
3. Press <kbd>Enter</kbd> to apply (or <kbd>Esc</kbd> to cancel)

A valid value flashes green and the camera moves to the new pose; invalid input flashes red and the previous value is restored. Editing **P** repositions the camera while keeping it aimed at the current target, while editing **T** re-aims the camera at a new target without moving it.

This is handy for reproducing exact viewpoints - for example, returning to a precise camera setup or sharing coordinates with someone else working on the same scene.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Keyboard Shortcuts

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/keyboard-shortcuts/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/keyboard-shortcuts.md

Open **Help > Keyboard Shortcuts** in the Editor for the in-app reference. The tables below list the default bindings.

On macOS, shortcuts shown with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> use <kbd>Cmd</kbd> for application commands such as Undo and Select All. The <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> selection modifier remains <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> on every platform.

## Editing and Selection

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Undo | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> |
| Redo | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Z</kbd> |
| Select all | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd> |
| Select none | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>A</kbd> |
| Invert selection | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd> |
| Delete selected Gaussians | <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> | <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> |
| Lock selection | <kbd>H</kbd> | <kbd>H</kbd> |
| Unlock all | <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd> | <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>H</kbd> |
| Toggle X-Ray | <kbd>N</kbd> | <kbd>N</kbd> |

For Rectangle, Lasso, Polygon, Brush, Sphere Brush, Flood, and Eyedropper selections, hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> to add, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> to remove, or <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Ctrl</kbd> to intersect with the current selection. [Selection Mode and X-Ray](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/editing-splats.md#selection-mode-and-x-ray) explains what <kbd>N</kbd> and <kbd>M</kbd> change.

## Tools and View

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Move / Rotate / Scale | <kbd>1</kbd> / <kbd>2</kbd> / <kbd>3</kbd> (while Box or Sphere Selection is active, these switch the selection volume's gizmo instead) |
| Rectangle / Lasso / Polygon Selection | <kbd>R</kbd> / <kbd>L</kbd> / <kbd>P</kbd> |
| Brush / Sphere Brush Selection | <kbd>B</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>B</kbd> |
| Flood Selection | <kbd>O</kbd> |
| Eyedropper Selection | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd> on macOS) |
| Decrease / increase brush size | <kbd>[</kbd> / <kbd>]</kbd>, or <kbd>Alt</kbd> + mouse wheel |
| Close the polygon | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Remove the last polygon point | <kbd>Backspace</kbd> |
| Remove the active Measure or Orient point | <kbd>Delete</kbd> or <kbd>Backspace</kbd> |
| Deactivate current tool | <kbd>Esc</kbd> |
| Toggle world/local coordinates | <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd> |
| Toggle Centers/Rings mode | <kbd>M</kbd> |
| Toggle markers | <kbd>Tab</kbd> |
| Toggle grid | <kbd>G</kbd> |
| Toggle camera info | <kbd>I</kbd> |
| Toggle Splat Data panel | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>D</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>D</kbd> on macOS) |
| Toggle Timeline panel | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> (<kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>T</kbd> on macOS) |

## Camera

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Frame the selection or active splat | <kbd>F</kbd> (frames the active Box, Sphere, Measure, or Orient tool instead while one is active) |
| Reset camera | <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd> |
| Toggle orbit/fly controls | <kbd>V</kbd> |
| Fly forward/back/left/right | <kbd>W</kbd> / <kbd>S</kbd> / <kbd>A</kbd> / <kbd>D</kbd> |
| Fly down/up | <kbd>Q</kbd> / <kbd>E</kbd> |
| Fly faster / slower | Hold <kbd>Shift</kbd> / <kbd>Alt</kbd> |

See [Camera Controls](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/editor/camera-controls.md) for mouse, touch, fly, and view-cube controls.

## Timeline

| Action | Shortcut |
|---|---|
| Play or pause | <kbd>Space</kbd> |
| Previous / next frame | <kbd>,</kbd> / <kbd>.</kbd> |
| Previous / next keyframe | <kbd>&lt;</kbd> / <kbd>&gt;</kbd> (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>,</kbd> / <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>.</kbd>) |
| Add keyframe | <kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Remove keyframe | <kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Enter</kbd> |
| Overwrite a keyframe with the current camera pose | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>-click the keyframe |
| Copy a keyframe | <kbd>Shift</kbd>-drag the keyframe |

## File

| Action | Windows/Linux | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Re-export (repeat the last export) | <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd> | <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>E</kbd> |

Shortcuts are ignored while focus is in a text or numeric input. The brush size shortcuts act on whichever brush is active; Brush and Sphere Brush share one size.

## Explore

URL: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/explore/
Markdown: https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/explore.md

The [Explore page](https://superspl.at) is the public-facing home of SuperSplat — an infinite-scroll gallery of every **Public** splat published on the platform. It's where visitors discover scenes without needing an account.

[Image: The SuperSplat Explore page — a grid of public splats]

Browsing Explore is **anonymous** — no PlayCanvas account is required. An account becomes useful when you want to [like](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md#likes), [comment](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md#comments), or [publish your own splats](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/upload.md).

## Feed tabs

The home page feed is split into tabs:

| Tab | What it shows |
|-----|---------------|
| **Trending** (default) | Splats gaining the most traction right now. |
| **Latest** (`?tab=latest`) | The most recently published splats. |
| **Following** (`?tab=following`) | Public splats from the creators you follow, newest first. Only shown while you're signed in. See [Following creators](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/user-profile.md#following). |

## The grid

Splats are shown as cards with a thumbnail, title, and author. Click a card to open the splat's [scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md).

The grid loads progressively as you scroll — the first page returns 32 splats (a 4×8 layout), and each subsequent page returns 16 (2×8). There's no "next page" button; just keep scrolling.

## Sorting, filtering, and search

Explore is driven entirely by URL parameters, so any filtered view is a shareable link.

### Sort (`?sort=...`)

| Value | Order |
|-------|-------|
| `trending` (default) | Splats gaining the most traction right now |
| `newest` | Most recently published first |
| `oldest` | Oldest first |
| `views` | Most-viewed first |
| `likes` | Most-liked first |
| `largest` | Largest file size first |
| `smallest` | Smallest file size first |

**Trending** is the default view at [superspl.at](https://superspl.at). It ranks splats by a recency-weighted engagement score — recent likes and views count for the most (engagement from the past week or so carries the most weight), with likes weighted above views — and is refreshed periodically, so the page surfaces what's popular *now* rather than all-time favourites.

:::note

Trending already accounts for recency, so it ignores the **time window** below — that control is hidden while Trending is selected.

:::

### Time window (`?time=...`)

Restricts the result set to splats published within a window. This applies to every sort **except `trending`** (the default), which always spans all time — selecting Trending hides the time control and clears any `?time=` value from the URL. For the other sorts the window defaults to `month` (the last 30 days).

| Value | Window |
|-------|--------|
| `month` | Last 30 days |
| `day` | Last 24 hours |
| `week` | Last 7 days |
| `year` | Last 12 months |
| `all` | No time restriction |

### Feature filters (`?features=...`)

Comma-separated list. The available filters are:

| Value | Splats matching |
|-------|-----------------|
| `walkable` | Splats with [collision](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/studio/collision.md) — visitors can walk through them |
| `downloadable` | Splats whose creators have enabled [downloads](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md#downloadable--license) |

### Search (`?q=...`)

The top-nav search bar adds a `q=` parameter that matches against splat **title** and **description**.

### Combined example

`https://superspl.at/?sort=likes&time=month&features=walkable&q=museum`

> Most-liked walkable splats published in the last month whose title or description mentions "museum."

## Creator profiles

Click a card's author chip to land on that user's [profile page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/user-profile.md) — a grid of every Public splat that user has shared, plus their avatar, bio, and social links. From there you can [follow them](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/user-profile.md#following) to see their new splats in your Following tab.

## See also

- [Scene page](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/scene-page.md) — what happens when you click a card
- [User Profile](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/viewing/user-profile.md) — browse one creator's published splats
- [Manage](https://developer.playcanvas.com/user-manual/supersplat/publishing/manage.md) — set your splats to **Public** so they appear in Explore
